stories.title: Lucknow fire survivor left paralysed after jumping from building:Legs numb, ribs fractured and lungs damaged; 7 doctors fight to save him
stories.summary: Jayant Gupta, who jumped from the second floor of a building to save his life during the Lucknow fire tragedy, has been fighting for survival for the past four days. A severe spinal cord injury has left the lower half of his body numb. Jayant is undergoing treatment at King George's Medical University (KGMU), where specialists from seven departments are monitoring his condition. Severe spinal cord injury leaves legs paralysed Dr Avdhesh Yadav, a neurosurgery expert at KGMU, told Dainik Bhaskar that the road to recovery will be extremely challenging for Jayant. According to Dr Yadav- 'Jayant has fractures in both legs. His legs have become paralysed and are completely numb. This is known as a complete cord injury. The chances of recovery are very low. It remains to be seen how much improvement occurs over time.' However, the doctor expressed hope that Jayant may eventually be able to stand on his own feet again. Jayant fell directly onto an iron grille after jumping from the building. He sustained critical injuries and lost consciousness before being rushed to KGMU's Trauma Centre. See in 3 pictures how Jayant saved his life- Rib fractures and lung injuries detected Doctors said Jayant suffered multiple rib fractures. The 10th rib on the right side and the 9th rib on the left side were severely damaged, causing injuries to his lungs as well. As a result, he has been provided ICD support (Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator) and remains under observation in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Both of his hands were also badly burnt during the incident. A severe injury at the D-10 level of the spinal cord has resulted in paraplegia. Doctors also found blood accumulation around both lungs (bilateral haemothorax) along with multiple rib fractures. He was in a state of shock when admitted to hospital. MRI reveals extensive damage An MRI scan revealed a serious ligament injury in the spine between the D-9 and D-11 vertebral levels. Doctors also detected- Dr Yadav said a multidisciplinary panel of experts has been formed to oversee Jayant's treatment. The team includes specialists from- Experts from other departments will also be consulted if required. Doctors say their primary goal is to ensure Jayant receives the best possible care and recovers as quickly as possible. Treatment provided so far According to hospital officials, Jayant is receiving comprehensive medical care, including oxygen support and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Doctors have conducted- Meanwhile, the plastic surgery team is treating his burn injuries. Conscious and stable in ICU Doctors said Jayant is fully conscious and responding appropriately to medical instructions. His blood pressure and other vital parameters remain stable. He is breathing normally without assistance and does not require ventilator support. His oxygen saturation level has been recorded at 96 per cent while breathing room air. A talented animation artist Jayant had been working at Head Hopper Studio since June 2022. Over the years, he developed expertise in hard-surface 3D modelling and texturing. More recently, he had focused on character modelling for animation projects. He learned animation at MAAC India and created several notable 3D character designs, including Textured Carbine and Wonder Woman. Key facts about Jayant Jump that saved his life Jayant was working on the second floor of Head Hopper Studio when the fire broke out. As flames engulfed the building and escape routes became inaccessible, he jumped from the second floor in an attempt to save himself. He landed on an iron grille and sustained life-threatening injuries. Although he survived the blaze, all 15 people who remained trapped inside the building lost their lives.

stories.title: Suspected Ram Mandir attack plot foiled:UP man arrested in Karnataka; ATS claims links to Pakistan-based terror group
stories.summary: A suspected terrorist allegedly plotting to blow up the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was arrested by the ATS and NIA in Karnataka on Wednesday evening. The accused, identified as Mohammad Suhail (22), is a resident of Gangoh in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district and was working in a factory in Karnataka. The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) claims that Suhail had links with a Pakistan-based terrorist organisation. Investigators say he had been living in Davangere, Karnataka, while concealing his identity, although the exact manner in which he did so remains unclear. Agencies have reportedly recovered Pakistani phone numbers, suspicious WhatsApp group links, and photographs showing him with weapons from his mobile phone. Officers from the NIA and ATS are currently interrogating him, and he may soon be brought to Uttar Pradesh for further questioning. Lead emerged during interrogation of two suspected terrorists According to sources, ATS recently arrested two suspected terrorists, Zameer Khan (22) from Davangere and Alla Baksh (24) from Tumakuru. During questioning, both allegedly disclosed Suhail's name. Acting on this information, ATS launched an operation and arrested him. Preliminary investigations suggest that Suhail was in contact with Pakistani terrorists through social media platforms. What did investigators find on Suhail's mobile phone? Officials say that during interrogation, Suhail admitted discussing plans to attack the Ram Mandir. Investigating agencies claim to have recovered photographs of him posing with weapons from his mobile phone. These images have been sent for forensic examination. In addition, officers reportedly found phone numbers bearing Pakistan's country code and several audio clips. In some of these recordings, Suhail is allegedly heard discussing plans to target the Ram Mandir. Taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation Davangere Superintendent of Police (SP) Shekhar HT said intelligence agencies had already received inputs regarding Suhail's activities. Following these inputs, a joint operation was carried out by Deputy SP Basavaraj of Davangere Rural Sub-Division, the Central Intelligence Agency, and the Davangere Crime Branch team. Suhail was arrested from Bannikodu village in Davangere district and is being taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation. Suhail's father, Liaqat, said he works as a labourer and has nine children — five daughters and four sons. Suhail is the youngest among all his siblings. All five daughters are married. His eldest brother, Ayaz, works as a driver in Saudi Arabia. The second brother, Shoaib, lives at home and is currently unemployed. The third brother, Jamil, works in the hosiery industry in Delhi. Suhail is the youngest and fourth son in the family. Worked as a labourer before going to Karnataka According to Suhail's father Liaqat, he studied at a madrasa up to Year 5. He previously worked as a daily-wage labourer. On 6 June, he travelled to Karnataka through a contractor to work as a painter. Liaqat claimed that Suhail was "mentally unstable" and had a strong desire to become famous on Instagram. He added- "I do not know what happened after he went to Karnataka. stories.title: Sindhi body claims 200 kg silver handed to Champat Rai:No receipt issued yet from Ram Mandir; 'Kakabhushundi' idol also missing
stories.summary: New allegations are surfacing daily in the Shri Ram Temple offerings theft case in Ayodhya. The Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam of Mumbai has claimed it has not received a receipt for the 200 kg of silver it donated, nor has the trust disclosed how the silver was used. A woman has also alleged that she was not given a receipt for donating a silver idol of Kakabhushundi. Both donations were reportedly handed over to Champat Rai, the temple trust’s general secretary. Meanwhile, Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony of the Sheshavatar Temple in the complex on June 23. Their presence has fueled speculation that all three may receive a clean chit in the offerings theft case. Read this report 200 Sindhis from 15 countries had donated silver slabs Dr. Raju Manwani, Chairman of Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam, told Dainik Bhaskar that At the time of temple construction, the whole world was donating. The Sindhi community also decided to donate 20-25 kg of silver. However, 200 people from the Sindhi community living in more than 15 countries were ready to donate one kilogram of silver each. After collecting 200 kg of silver bricks, we contacted Champat Rai. He took the bricks and called us to Ayodhya. 200 people from the community reached Ayodhya with the bricks on January 26, 2021. After the worship of the bricks, they were handed over to Champat Rai. Dr. Raju Manwani said, All the bricks had pictures of Lord Jhulelal and other deities. Champat Rai said that after checking the purity of the bricks, a receipt would be sent. He also assured that we would be informed where the bricks would be used.Today it has been five years, but no receipt has been given by the Trust. Neither did anyone call, nor did we receive any response on our phones. After the case of theft of offerings came to light, I have received calls from many people in the community. They want to know where the donated 200 kg of silver has been used. Silver Kakabhushundi idol also missing A woman named Anita Bhardwaj has also accused them of not providing a receipt for donated silver. The woman claims that she gave a silver idol of Kakabhushundi (a sage in the form of a crow) to Champat Rai in Karsevakpuram. She had requested him to give it a place in the Ram Darbar. Champat Rai had said that cameras are not allowed inside. Photos and receipts will be sent later. After this, Anita wrote several letters to Champat Rai asking for the receipt, but she has not received it to date. She was also not told anything about that idol. 5 suspects imprisoned in Ram Mandir complex The initial investigation in the offering theft case was conducted by the Trust itself. It is being claimed that the Trust has seized approximately 2 crore rupees and jewelry from the homes and stated locations of several personnel by June 13. Since then, the suspects Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Avinash, Karunesh, and Manish Yadav have been kept within the temple premises. Their mobile phones have also been confiscated. The SIT has also interrogated them. Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, who was formerly the driver of General Secretary Champat Rai, has also been kept on the premises. However, he is allowed to move freely anywhere within the premises. He is also using a mobile phone. Whereas, Tinnu is still being described as the main figure in the offering theft case. The recovery of jewelry from his house has also come to light. The temple administrators are living in the temple premises as before. Champat Rai is also living in the temple. Earlier, he used to live in the VHP office located in Karsevakpuram. Dr. Anil Mishra is commuting from his home. All three trustees likely to get a clean chit In the offerings theft case, the roles of General Secretary Champat Rai, counting in-charge and trust member Dr Anil Mishra, and manager Gopal Rao are under scrutiny. Former temple accountant Mahipal and former engineer Dinanath Verma have alleged that Champat Rai was aware of both the theft of offerings and a 40% commission in the purchase of construction materials. They claim they informed him, but instead of taking action, both were removed from temple duties. Mumbai businessman Anil Vishwakarma has accused Champat Rai of not issuing receipts for a Dwadash Jyotirling necklace and foot-pads donated to the temple. The SIT has recorded statements from Vishwakarma and Guru Acharya Vinod Mishra, while the Indian Bullion Jewellers Association has also raised questions over 60 kg of silver bricks. During his recent visit to Ayodhya, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reportedly kept all three individuals away from official programmes. However, Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony at Sheshavatar Temple on 23 June. Champat Rai led the event and delivered a speech, fuelling claims that all three have received a clean chit in the SIT's preliminary report.

stories.title: Heavy rain in Prayagraj, alert issued for 26 districts:Temperature crosses 44°C, heat and humidity intensify
stories.summary: The spell of fluctuating weather conditions continues across Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in Prayagraj early on Thursday, while light drizzle occurred in Meerut. Most cities across the state witnessed bright sunshine from the morning onwards. With wind speeds remaining low, heat and humidity levels have increased significantly. Rain and heatwave alerts issued The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 26 districts and a heatwave warning for eight districts on Thursday. Strong winds with speeds of up to 60 kmph are also likely during this period. Monsoon Expected to Enter UP Within 2–3 Days There is some relief on the monsoon front, with weather officials indicating that the southwest monsoon could enter Uttar Pradesh within the next two to three days. The monsoon is expected to enter the state through the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj region via the Bihar border by 28 June. According to forecasts- Typically, the monsoon reaches Uttar Pradesh by around 20 June. This year, however, it is running approximately eight days behind schedule. The monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj for the past 15 days. Banda records highest temperature During the past 24 hours, Banda was the hottest location in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 44.2°C. Several districts experienced heavy rainfall, including- In Agra, strong winds during the evening caused a roadside utility pole to collapse onto parked cars. The rear portions of two vehicles were crushed in the incident. Lucknow Meteorological Centre scientist Atul Kumar Singh said the southwest monsoon became active over parts of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on June 23. He said the monsoon is expected to advance over the remaining parts of the North Arabian Sea, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand over the next two to three days. This could allow it to reach parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar within the next three to four days. How will the weather for the next five days ? 26 June: Dry weather is expected across eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, with temperatures likely to rise. 27 June: Heatwave conditions are expected to persist across the state. Hot winds may intensify discomfort, especially in eastern Uttar Pradesh. 28 June: Western Uttar Pradesh is likely to remain dry, while eastern districts may receive rain. 29 June: Light rain is likely in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern parts may witness heavy rainfall. 30 June: Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected in western Uttar Pradesh. Eastern Uttar Pradesh may experience strong storms along with widespread rainfall.

stories.title: 'Dead bodies found holding each other's hands':Firefighters recount horror inside Lucknow's deadly blaze
stories.summary: Officers, firefighters and police personnel, who were part of the rescue team in Lucknow fire tragedy, have revealed chilling details about the operation. The fire, which erupted on 22 June at Head Hopper Studio in Aliganj area, claimed 15 lives. The Bhaskar Investigation Team spoke to members of the rescue team to recount how the operation unfolded. They described the life-threatening conditions they faced, the challenges that slowed the rescue, and the haunting scenes they witnessed inside the smoke-filled building. Here's what they said: The entire building was engulfed in thick smoke. The rear wall and several windows had been blown apart. Wearing breathing apparatus, we climbed to the second floor using ropes. Inside, visibility was almost zero. Even our torchlights were ineffective. We could only move forward by instinct. The broken windowpanes allowed some of the smoke to escape, creating a narrow path for us to enter the Head Hopper Studio. What we found inside was horrifying. Every time our feet brushed against a body, we realised that someone was lying on the floor. Victims were found inside cabins and washrooms. Some bodies were slumped against walls. One person's head was bent to one side while the body had collapsed in another direction. A young man was found with his hand covering his mouth, his body leaning against a wall. It appeared he had tried to shield himself from the smoke but could not survive. First, 3 pictures of the firefighters who carried out the rescue Now read what the firefighters are saying Case 1: AC outdoor units blocked the staircase, forcing rescuers to enter from the rear A constable from Madiyaon police station, among the first to reach the spot, said the rescue operation was hampered from the very beginning. "Eight to ten AC outdoor units had been installed along the narrow staircase leading into the building. Several motorcycles and scooters parked there had also caught fire. The flames and thick smoke quickly engulfed the only entrance, making the passage even narrower." According to him, firefighters initially tried to douse the blaze from the front, but there was no way to enter the building. There were no windows or alternative openings through which rescuers could reach those trapped inside. Some firefighters climbed onto the roof by placing a ladder against the neighbouring building. They hoped to enter through the rooftop staircase, but found the access door secured with a heavy lock that could not be broken from above. With every route blocked, the rescue team decided to breach the rear wall. The building had only one entry and exit point, and that too was obstructed by AC outdoor units, making the rescue operation significantly more difficult. Case 2: A 9-inch wall stood between rescuers and the trapped victims The fireman involved in breaching the rear wall said it appeared to be the quickest way to reach those trapped inside. "The wall was around nine inches thick and reinforced with heavy plaster. It was extremely strong." A drilling machine was brought to the site, but it could not be operated because the electricity supply had already been disconnected. With no time to lose, Constable Mayank, posted at Madiyaon police station, picked up a heavy sledgehammer. "Waiting for the machine was not an option. We believed breaking the wall was the only way to save those inside. I kept striking the wall continuously until it finally gave way," he said. Once the opening was created, firefighters gained access to the building through two breaches made in the rear wall. It was through these openings that the rescue operation progressed. Later, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak visited the site to inspect the breached wall. Case 3: 'Visibility was zero; we found bodies only after stumbling over them' The first firefighter to enter the building described conditions inside as almost impossible. "When we stepped inside, nothing was visible. The smoke was so dense that even our torchlights were ineffective. We could only move forward by instinct, feeling our way with each step." He said rescuers often realised someone was lying on the floor only after their boots brushed against a body. Because of the dense smoke and the building's maze-like layout, firefighters tied themselves together with ropes before entering. "We stayed connected throughout the operation. There was a constant fear that someone from the team could lose their way inside. The ropes ensured that no one got separated." After the rear wall was breached, rescue teams entered the building and recovered 15 bodies. Case 4: Cabins became smoke traps; victims were found across the studio A firefighter involved in recovering the bodies said the second floor had been divided into multiple cabins using glass partitions. "The smoke spread into every section of the studio. We found bodies in almost every cabin. Some victims had collapsed near the doors, while others were found inside enclosed rooms." Several bodies were found lying close together. "Their hands were touching each other, almost as if they had been holding hands. It looked like a scene from a film." One young man was found sitting against a wall with his hand covering his mouth, apparently trying to protect himself from the smoke. Another victim was discovered inside a washroom. Bodies of young men and women were scattered across the studio. Case 5: 'Better ventilation could have saved lives' The police officer leading the rescue operation believes the building's design turned the fire into a deadly trap. "If the building had adequate windows, exhaust systems or proper ventilation, much of the smoke could have escaped. Perhaps many lives could have been saved." He said the structure was almost completely sealed except for the front entrance. "There were virtually no windows. The smoke remained trapped inside, making survival difficult for those trapped and preventing rescuers from reaching them quickly." Rescue operation at a glance

stories.title: Pratapgarh’s Rohit Mishra set to become BJYM UP Chief:Linked to Keshav Maurya’s rival camp; Usha Maurya leads women’s wing race
stories.summary: The BJP’s Uttar Pradesh organisational team may be announced soon. According to sources, the name of Rohit Mishra is almost final for the post of state president of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM). A former Allahabad University Students’ Union president, Rohit is currently serving as BJYM state vice-president. Rohit Mishra is considered close to former Prayagraj MLA Udaybhan Karwariya. Karwariya is known to be a vocal critic of Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya. Meanwhile, the names of Ranjana Upadhyay, Archana Mishra and Usha Maurya are being discussed for the post of BJP Mahila Morcha state president. Sources say that if Rohit Mishra is appointed BJYM chief, Usha Maurya could be made the state president of the women’s wing. Wife of GST officer may get the post The BJP’s 45-member state team currently includes 12 women, accounting for around 26% representation. To raise the women’s quota to 33%, the number of women office-bearers could be increased to 14. The list of state office-bearers may also include the wives of GST and Customs officials. BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary is the Union Minister of State for Finance and oversees the Customs and GST departments. Bina Lavania and Sanchita Chauhan, wives of Indian Revenue Service officers, are also said to be in the race for organisational posts. Owner of Dayal Hotel also in the race for state team Businessmen from Lucknow’s hospitality and automobile sectors are also reportedly vying for positions in the BJP state unit. Rajesh Singh Dayal, owner of Dayal Gateway Hotel, and Jatin Verma, who runs JSV Automobile showroom, are among those being considered for organisational posts. Jatin Verma’s candidature is reportedly being backed on the grounds that he was part of the party’s election management team. According to sources, most names on the list have been included based on the preference of Pankaj Chaudhary. A few names have also been recommended by Deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, as well as BJP state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh. Deliberations over the BJP’s Uttar Pradesh team have been underway for the past four months, from Lucknow to New Delhi. After consultations with RSS functionaries in the state, multiple rounds of discussions were held in Delhi involving national president Nitin Nabin, national general secretary (organisation) B.L. Santhosh and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Sources say the list has now been finalised after taking caste and regional equations into account. Life-threatening attack on Rohit occurred 2 years ago Around two years ago, BJYM state vice-president Rohit Mishra survived an alleged murderous attack in Prayagraj. In his police complaint, Rohit stated that he was walking outside his house around 1.15 am after dinner when several men stepped out of a Safari vehicle, abused him and surrounded him. He alleged that they first tried to run him over with the vehicle and later assaulted him with iron rods. Despite repeatedly asking why he was being attacked, he received no answer. According to Rohit, the assailants kept saying, “You don’t know who we are. We will teach you a lesson for your politics.”

stories.title: AAP protests in Lucknow over Ram Temple donation scam:Alleges ₹14,000-crore donation fraud; demands FIR against Champat Rai
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) staged a protest in Lucknow on Saturday over the alleged donation theft case linked to Ayodhya’s Shri Ram Temple. Party workers gathered at the Swasthya Bhawan intersection in Kaiserbagh and marched towards Hazratganj from the Collectorate side while raising slogans and carrying banners reading, “Donation Thieves, Vacate Your Posts.” Police stopped the protesters during the march. 'CCTV Video Was Deleted' District Secretary Gyan Singh said the Yogi government was refusing to acknowledge the alleged Ram Temple donation theft. “Our Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh has repeatedly presented evidence showing how the theft took place. There has been a scam involving land worth crores of rupees,” he alleged. He further claimed that there was no proper accounting of the money allegedly missing from donation boxes. “Photographs and videos from CCTV cameras were deleted in an attempt to destroy evidence,” he alleged. 'Theft of 14000 crores' Gyan Singh alleged that the entire trust was involved in corruption and irregularities. “Action should be taken against all those involved. Instead of acting against a single individual, the entire trust should be replaced immediately. At least ₹14,000 crore has been stolen,” he claimed. He said devotees from India and abroad donate their hard-earned money to the temple. “No one knows how much undisclosed donation has been received. The trust should be dissolved immediately, a new trust should be formed, and criminal cases should be registered against all the accused. FIRs are not being filed because their own people are involved,” he alleged. ₹420 will be collected as donation from every district AAP leader Pratipal Singh said the party was protesting against the alleged theft linked to the Ram Temple. “Our party will collect ₹420 from every district and send it to Champat Rai. Crores of people have faith in the temple,” he said. Calling the alleged incident deeply shameful, Pratipal Singh said the party would prepare a demand draft of ₹420 and send it in Champat Rai’s name. “We want to tell him not to steal,” he remarked. He also said the party had no faith in the SIT investigation and demanded that the matter be probed by a retired Supreme Court judge.

stories.title: Yogi targets SP over law and order:Says harassers will face strict action, mafia era is over
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday said that during the Samajwadi Party (SP) government, every district in Uttar Pradesh had a mafia figure who would grab land, threaten traders and women, attack police personnel and tarnish the image of Bundelkhand. Addressing a public gathering in Hamirpur, Yogi said that there is no place for the mafia in Uttar Pradesh today. “The mafia are either in jail or have been reduced to dust. No one can now compromise the safety of daughters. If anyone dares to do so, they will be sent to Yamraj’s abode,” he said. Referring to the delayed monsoon, the Chief Minister said that although June 21 had arrived, the monsoon was yet to reach the state. “Since we have been travelling continuously, perhaps God thought the heat should not be too intense, which is why we are seeing some clouds. The monsoon was good over the last two years. However, warnings have already been issued that due to El Niño, there could be untimely and below-normal rainfall over the next three years. I appeal to everyone to save water,” he said. He further said that the Har Ghar Nal Yojana was aimed at ensuring proper use of drinking water. “People should not leave taps running unnecessarily. Water theft should not be allowed. We must prevent a drinking water crisis and use only as much water as required,” he said. The Chief Minister was in Hamirpur to inaugurate and lay the foundation stones of 75 development projects worth ₹636 crore. Earlier in the day, he inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 88 projects worth ₹697 crore in Mahoba. He also visited Gorakhgiri after 12 years and offered prayers to Lord Shiva. Key Highlights From CM Yogi’s Speech 1. Bundelkhand’s roads were full of potholes nine years ago Yogi said that nine years ago, roads in Bundelkhand were riddled with potholes, women spent their lives carrying water in pots and the youth struggled for recognition. “Mafia elements dominated the region and exploited the poor. Over the past 12 years, we have witnessed a changing India,” he said. 2. Those practising caste politics only serve their families The Chief Minister said that people across the world had celebrated International Yoga Day and that yoga was a gift of India’s ancient sage tradition. “In modern times, Prime Minister Narendra Modi secured global recognition for yoga. The world is now acknowledging India’s traditions. Earlier, caste-based politics created an identity crisis. Such leaders, when they come to power, only serve their families. For Prime Minister Modi, all 1.4 billion Indians are family,” he said. 3. Ammunition, artillery and missiles are now being manufactured in UP Yogi recalled his first visit to Bundelkhand after becoming Chief Minister in 2017 and said that at the time, discussions focused on improving connectivity and building the Bundelkhand Expressway. “Today, Bundelkhand has its own expressway. Earlier, soldiers from Bundelkhand served in the Army, but the ammunition they used was imported from different countries. That is no longer the case,” he said. “Today, ammunition, artillery and missiles are being manufactured in Uttar Pradesh. When the BrahMos missile made in Uttar Pradesh was fired at Pakistan, it was forced to retreat and was seen pleading for its life before the world.” He said the Har Ghar Nal Yojana had brought relief to women and daughters, while recruitment drives now provide opportunities for Bundelkhand’s youth as well. “Earlier, development schemes were designed keeping Saifai in mind,” he added. 4. Those who created an identity crisis for UP are now struggling for relevance The Chief Minister said that areas affected by mining should undertake plantation drives. “Previous governments exploited the people. We have moved beyond that phase. Uttar Pradesh no longer struggles for recognition. Those who once pushed the state into an identity crisis are now the ones searching for relevance. The public has rejected them,” he said. 5. Public money is no longer spent on cemetery boundary walls Yogi accused previous governments of appeasement politics. “Congress leaders used to claim that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna never existed. The Samajwadi Party ordered lathi charges and firing when people raised slogans of ‘Jai Shri Ram’. They tried to stop Krishna Janmotsav and Kanwar Yatra celebrations, while encouraging unruly behaviour on roads during Muharram and Eid. Today, public money is no longer spent on constructing cemetery boundary walls,” he said. 6. We had vowed to reduce the mafia to dust Earlier in Mahoba, the Chief Minister reiterated his government’s commitment to taking action against organised crime. “We had pledged to reduce the mafia to dust. We want this defence manufacturing hub to expand across Mahoba, Chitrakoot, Hamirpur and Jhansi. Industrial clusters are being developed for this purpose,” he said. Without naming the Samajwadi Party, he added that those who only knew how to encroach upon land could never contribute positively to society and had pushed the state backwards. 7. Akharas dedicated to Alha-Udal’s legacy will be developed Yogi announced that a ropeway would be built and Gorakhgiri would be developed as an adventure tourism destination. He said the Mahoba Mahotsav would feature competitions ranging from district-level to national-level events. Akharas symbolising the bravery of Alha and Udal would also be developed. “Maho ba will be given a new identity in line with its glorious heritage,” he said. 8. Earlier, mafia dominated and disturbances occurred before festivals The Chief Minister said that long-pending payments to farmers affected by the Kabrai Dam project had been cleared. “Strict action will be taken against those who exploit farmers. The countdown has begun for those exploiting the youth. Uttar Pradesh is now building a new identity. Earlier, mafia elements dominated society and disturbances occurred before festivals. Neither daughters nor traders felt safe. The districts existed then as well, but they suffered from an identity crisis. Through BIDA, Bundelkhand is now being given a global industrial identity,” he said. 9. Chitrakoot, Banda and Hamirpur will also witness transformation Yogi said the potential of Mahoba must be fully developed and that similar transformation would be brought to Chitrakoot, Banda and Hamirpur. “A medical college has already been established in Mahoba. Professionalism needs to be brought into the tourism sector. The double-engine government is continuously working on security and good governance, which pave the way for development,” he said. He added that Mahoba should reach new heights, the folk tales of Alha and Udal should gain global recognition and the fame of Desawari paan should continue to grow. “The government stands with you at every step. Mahoba will advance both development and heritage together,” he said.

stories.title: 'Bottle Baba' claimed he revived the dead:Gave woman a ‘blessed’ apple, promised she would bear a son
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, several videos of Bottle Baba, who was arrested on charges of molestation and whipping a female devotee, are now surfacing. In one video, he appears to be claiming to bring life back to an allegedly dead woman by catching her soul from the air, while in another video, he is seen blessing a childless woman with the promise of a son by blowing on her and giving her an apple. Actually, on Friday, Bottle Baba was sent to jail. A woman had complained that the Baba called her into a room at the ashram and attempted to rape her. When she escaped and came out, to prevent the Baba's truth from being exposed, he beat her up claiming she was possessed by an evil spirit. The woman has leveled charges against him including attempted rape, assault, attempted murder, and extortion of 40 thousand rupees. First see these 2 pictures Now know what is in both the videos that have surfaced... Video-1 In the first video that surfaced on social media, Bottle Baba is seen standing among followers in his ashram. In front of him, the alleged dead body of a young woman is lying. When asked, a woman present there says that she died due to kidney disease. After this, a woman from the ashram sprinkles water on the young woman's body. The Baba claims to catch the soul by waving his hand in the air and appears to make it enter the woman's body with a gesture of shooting an arrow. After some time, the young woman gets up and stands. The Baba says, "She had died. In the hospital, doctors took money from the family members, but I put her soul back into her body. How her life was saved, only I and Mother Kali know." After this, the people present there are seen clapping and chanting slogans. Video-2 A woman from Jalaun comes to the Baba's gathering and tells him that she has no children. She says that she had conceived earlier, but had a miscarriage. The Baba asks the woman to get an apple. He blows on it, recites mantras, and throws it in the woman's lap saying, "Whether the deficiency is in you or your husband, go beggar woman, you will be blessed with a son." After this, he instructs the woman to go under a tree, eat the entire apple, and ensure that no one sees her during this time. The woman touches the Baba's feet and leaves from there. Now know about Bottle Baba In the Devrahat police station area, at Haridhaam Sarkar Ashram located in Chain Ka Purwa village, Hariom Yadav used to hold court under the name 'Bottle Baba'. He would blow into water bottles, calling it nectar, and claimed to cure many serious diseases including cancer and kidney ailments. According to local people, people from far and wide would come to his gatherings. Many people considered him a miraculous saint, while some people have also been raising questions about his methods. Know how Bottle Baba was exposed A woman residing in a village in the Phaphund police station area of Auraiya had her father-in-law and two brothers-in-law call a Baba (godman) to their home on June 6 for worship rituals. The woman alleges that during the worship, the Baba said that she was under the influence of dark forces and that a special puja would need to be performed to remove it. According to the woman, during this time, 40 thousand rupees were taken from her. While leaving, the Baba called her to Haridham Sarkar Ashram on June 15. Allegation of molestation after being called into a room The woman alleges that on June 15, both her brothers-in-law brought her to the ashram on a bike. There, the Baba called her into a room under the pretext of a special ritual and attempted to rape her while committing obscene acts. When she resisted, the Baba, both brothers-in-law, and other people beat her up. The woman alleges that an attempt was also made to kill her by strangling her. The woman somehow managed to get out of the room, but people present there caught her. After this, the Baba took her to the congregation and told people that the woman was under the influence of ghosts and spirits and that was why she was running away. Forcibly kept asking names of ghosts In the viral video of about four minutes, the Baba is seen holding the woman and whipping her. He repeatedly asks her how many ghosts are with her. The woman keeps pleading with folded hands to be let go. The woman alleges that the Baba forcibly kept asking her the names of ghosts. She could not say anything due to fear. During this, she was struck with whips and sharp objects on her hands, legs and waist. She was beaten for about half an hour. Later she was sent home with her brothers-in-law. After this she reached the police and filed a complaint. The victim said- When the Baba molested me in the room, I ran outside. His disciples and both my brothers-in-law caught me. After this, the Baba took me to the congregation and started beating me claiming I was possessed by ghosts and spirits, so that people would believe his story and no one would believe my allegations. Case filed against Baba and 5 named and 5 unknown persons On the complaint of the woman, a case was registered on June 18 at Devrahat police station against Hariom Yadav, the woman's two brothers-in-law Ramvir and Sukhvir, the Baba's disciples Deepak and Kundan, along with several others under sections of molestation, assault and other charges. Taking action, the police arrested the Baba and one of his disciples. Baba said - A leader is conspiring to frame me Calling the allegations against him baseless, the Baba said, "False allegations have always been made against Sanatanists. Now false allegations are being made against me too. This is all a conspiracy. A leader from Dibiyapur, Ashish Dwivedi, is plotting to frame me. I don't have any small ashram. It is built on 8 bighas. The saint congregation will continue and no one can end the saint tradition." Ashram built on 8 bighas, entry given with water bottle Baba's ashram is built on about 8 bighas in Chain Ka Purwa village. It is said that earlier a receipt of 100 rupees was issued for worship, which later increased to 250 rupees. 100 to 200 people visit the darbar daily. It is said that buying a water bottle for 20 rupees is mandatory for entry here. Baba would blow into this water and claim it to be miraculous, asserting that even serious illnesses could be cured by it.

stories.title: Women narrowly escapes death in Unnao:Falls while boarding Amrapali Express, survives under moving train
stories.summary: In Unnao, UP, an entire train passed over a woman, but she narrowly escaped. She only suffered a minor scratch on her ear. What happened was that the woman was boarding the Amrapali Express train on Saturday night when her foot slipped and she fell onto the track. By then the train had picked up speed. 21 railway coaches passed over her. The woman lay curled up between the tracks. After the train passed, GRP-RPF lifted the woman and took her to the district hospital, where after primary treatment the woman was discharged. The incident occurred on platform number-2 of Unnao Junction. Woman's son narrated the entire incident Ramshila (48) is originally a resident of Amrapali village in Korba, Madhya Pradesh. In Unnao, she has been living for several months with her husband Gangaram, son Sagar and brother Jai. All of them work at a brick kiln in Achalganj. Son Sagar said - On Saturday night we were returning to our village. We had reached Unnao station to catch the train. According to Sagar, he had bought a ticket for the Amrapali Express. The train arrived at Platform-2 at around 12:10 AM at night. My father and I boarded the train with our luggage. Finally, mother was boarding, when her foot slipped and she fell onto the tracks between the train and the platform. When mother screamed while falling, my father and I got down from the train to save her, but by then the train had started moving. The son said - it was fortunate that mother was lying exactly in the middle of the tracks. All 21 bogies of the train passed over mother. God saved her. Woman appeared frightened after the accident After the accident, the woman appeared frightened for a long time. Even in the hospital, she kept holding her husband's hand. The husband kept reassuring her that nothing had happened to her. The doctors at the district hospital said - the woman is completely safe and conscious. She has a minor injury to her ear. After primary treatment, she has been discharged from the hospital. RPF Inspector Harish Kumar Meena said- The woman sustained minor injuries in the accident. RPF and GRP safely rescued her. I appeal to passengers not to attempt to board or alight from a moving train. Even a little carelessness can lead to a major accident.

stories.title: UP-bound AC sleeper bus catches fire on Ludhiana highway:Panic among 80 passengers; all luggage destroyed
stories.summary: A moving sleeper bus carrying around 80 passengers, including women and children, catches fire on the Ludhiana-Amritsar National Highway near Khanna in Punjab on Sunday. The bus is travelling from Jalandhar to Gonda district in Uttar Pradesh when the incident occurs near Bija village. According to officials, the fire breaks out suddenly and spreads rapidly through the vehicle. Within minutes, flames engulf the entire bus, triggering panic among passengers. The driver immediately pulls the bus to the roadside, while the conductor begins evacuating passengers. All passengers are brought out safely, helping avert a major tragedy. Passengers leave belongings behind as fire spreads As the fire intensifies, passengers rush out of the bus amid chaos and screams. Some passengers suffer minor burns and injuries while trying to escape. They receive first aid at the spot. The blaze spreads so quickly that passengers do not get time to collect their belongings. Luggage stored inside the bus is completely destroyed in the fire. Police and administrative officials reach the site soon after receiving information about the incident. SDM reviews rescue operations Khanna SDM Swati Tiwana visits the spot and reviews the relief and rescue efforts. She says the administration responds immediately after receiving information about the fire. "All passengers are safe. The bus has been completely reduced to ashes," she says. Tiwana says preliminary findings suggest the fire may have been caused by a short circuit. Officials estimate that around 100 passengers are travelling in the bus. The administration is preparing a list of passengers and gathering details about their boarding points and destinations. The administration provides necessary assistance and makes arrangements to transport passengers to safe locations. Fire brought under control with two tenders Fire department teams reach the spot and launch firefighting operations. However, the bus is completely gutted before the flames are brought under control. Fire officer Kiranveer Singh says two fire tenders are deployed immediately after the department receives information about the incident. "The cause of the fire is under investigation. All passengers are safe. The fire is brought under control with the help of two fire brigade vehicles," he says. Police say the fire is initially suspected to have been caused by a technical fault, but the exact reason will be known only after a detailed investigation. No casualties are reported in the incident, though passengers suffer heavy financial losses as their belongings are destroyed in the fire.

stories.summary: The NEET-UG 2026 re-examination begins across Uttar Pradesh on Sunday with around 3.5 lakh candidates appearing for the test. Entry at examination centres starts at 11 am and continues till 1.30 pm, while the exam is scheduled from 2 pm to 5.15 pm. Authorities put strict security arrangements in place at all centres. Candidates are allowed entry only after verification of admit cards, valid photo identity documents, photographs, signatures and biometric details. The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts the re-exam after cancelling the earlier test due to a paper leak. The original examination was held on May 3 and was cancelled on May 12.

stories.title: Speeding Thar kills youth returning from hospital in Lucknow:Victim thrown nearly 100 feet; had just met injured brother
stories.summary: A 26-year-old man died after a speeding Thar hit him in Lucknow's Kakori area on Saturday night. The impact was so strong that he was thrown nearly 100 feet away and died on the spot. The deceased, identified as Himalaya, was the elder son of Shivmangal, a resident of Mandoli village. Returning from hospital when accident occurs According to police and local residents, Himalaya had gone to Era Hospital in Balanganj on Saturday evening to meet his younger brother Himanshu and deliver food. Himanshu is undergoing treatment after suffering injuries in a fall from a mango tree a few days ago. After leaving the hospital, Himalaya returned by auto and got down near Golakua village. He was crossing Hardoi Road and walking towards Mandoli village at around 9 pm when a speeding Thar coming from the Malihabad side allegedly hit him. The collision threw him into the air before he landed on the road at a considerable distance. He died at the scene. Villagers rushed to the spot after learning about the incident. Villagers stage protest, block road for three hours Angered by the death, villagers placed the body on the road and staged a protest. The road blockade continued for nearly three hours, until around midnight. The protesters demanded compensation for the family and the immediate arrest of the driver involved in the accident. The protest caused a traffic jam of nearly 1.5 kilometres on Hardoi Road. Driver flees after accident Residents said the black Thar was moving at high speed when it hit Himalaya. The driver allegedly fled the spot with the vehicle immediately after the accident. Police have launched efforts to trace the vehicle and identify the driver. Family seeks compensation and government job Family members and villagers demanded compensation of ₹1 crore, stating that Himalaya was the sole earning member of the household. They also sought a government job for one member of the family. Himalaya is survived by his injured younger brother Himanshu and two sisters, Himanshi and Ragini. Police register case Kakori Inspector Satish Chandra Rathore reached the spot and assured the family that all eligible compensation would be provided as per rules. Following the assurance, the protesters ended the road blockade. Police from Kakori and Dubagga police stations jointly held talks with the family and local residents before restoring normal traffic movement. The body has been sent for post-mortem examination. Based on a complaint filed by the victim's father, Shivmangal, Kakori police have registered a case under sections related to rash and negligent driving that endangers life.

stories.title: Delayed monsoon scorches UP:Sprinklers installed for animals in zoo; 31 cities face heatwave conditions
stories.summary: The delayed arrival of the monsoon has intensified heat across Uttar Pradesh. Most cities are witnessing strong sunshine on Sunday, while low wind speeds have increased humidity levels. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has not forecast widespread rainfall, although intermittent cloud movement may bring light drizzle in some areas. The monsoon remains stalled near the UP-Bihar border and has been stationary around Maharajganj for the past 8-9 days. According to the IMD, the system may start advancing again from June 23 and could enter Uttar Pradesh by June 25. Animals struggle with heat in Gorakhpur and Kanpur zoos The soaring temperatures are affecting animals as well. In Gorakhpur Zoo, a tigress spends most of the day inside a swimming pool and comes out only after temperatures fall in the evening. In Kanpur Zoo, sprinklers have been installed for a rhinoceros to help it cope with the heat. The animal is frequently seen standing under water sprays during the day. Heatwave alert issued for 31 districts The IMD has issued a heatwave alert for 31 districts on Sunday. Hot winds and above-normal temperatures are likely to continue in several parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand until the monsoon arrives. The districts under alert include Banda, Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, Prayagraj, Fatehpur, Pratapgarh, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli, Varanasi, Sant Ravidas Nagar, Jaunpur, Ghazipur, Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Gonda, Shravasti, Bahraich, Lakhimpur Kheri, Sitapur, Hardoi, Kanpur Nagar, Unnao, Lucknow, Barabanki, Rae Bareli, Amethi, Sultanpur, Ayodhya and Ambedkar Nagar. Banda hottest in the country; rain brings brief relief in six cities On Saturday, rainfall was recorded in six cities, including Lucknow, Hathras and Sonbhadra, providing temporary relief from the heat. However, Banda remained the hottest place in the country, recording a maximum temperature of 43.2°C. Severe heat likely for next 3-4 days Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said Uttar Pradesh is likely to witness severe heat for the next three to four days. Temperatures are expected to rise further, worsening heatwave conditions. He said the monsoon's progress remains slow and conditions are not yet favourable for its arrival in the state. According to him, people may have to wait at least five more days for monsoon relief. Weather outlook for next five days UP may receive 8% below-normal rainfall this season Senior scientist Atul Singh said Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive below-normal rainfall this year. The state generally records 820-840 mm of rainfall between June and September. However, this year's total rainfall is projected to remain around 754-773 mm, nearly 8% below normal. El Niño conditions may weaken monsoon IMD Director General Dr M. Mahapatra said conditions in the Pacific Ocean are showing signs of shifting towards El Niño after the end of La Niña-like conditions. He said this transition could reduce rainfall during the southwest monsoon season. Lower snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March may also affect monsoon performance this year. Impact on agriculture and prices Below-normal rainfall could affect agriculture, the rural economy and household budgets across the state. Paddy production may decline by up to 20%, while delayed rainfall in June and July could postpone transplantation and reduce the cultivated area. Farmers may have to depend more on tube wells for irrigation, increasing electricity and diesel expenses. Lower crop output could push up prices of grains, pulses and vegetables. Drought concerns may also intensify in Bundelkhand and south-western Uttar Pradesh districts such as Jhansi, Mahoba, Lalitpur and Mathura. Last year, UP received excess monsoon rainfall According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh recorded 870-900 mm of rainfall during the 2025 monsoon season, around 10-15% higher than the state's normal seasonal average.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation case- SIT to submit report to Yogi:Warning issued to 150 individuals, including Champat Rai not to leave Ayodhya
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir has completed its six-day investigation in Ayodhya and returned to Lucknow on Saturday evening. Sources indicate that the inquiry has brought around 150 individuals under suspicion, while action is likely against nearly 25 people. Those questioned during the investigation have been instructed not to leave their respective locations without prior permission until further orders. Preliminary report likely to be submitted to CM Yogi Following the completion of evidence collection, documentation, and recording of statements, the SIT is expected to submit its preliminary report to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath either late Sunday or on Monday. The team had attempted to meet the Chief Minister on Sunday evening; however, the meeting could not take place due to his prior engagements, including preparations for the Monsoon Session and other official meetings. Suspects under scrutiny and travel restrictions The SIT has directed all individuals who have been questioned so far to remain within their respective locations and not travel without permission until further instructions are issued. This forms part of the ongoing monitoring process following the investigation. Focus on key Mandir functionaries During the probe, investigators repeatedly questioned Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu, who is believed to hold significant influence within the Mandir administration. The SIT also gathered detailed information regarding his associates, relatives, and their property holdings. The investigation involved a detailed review of CCTV footage, donation handling records, cash-counting procedures, and the process of transferring offerings to banks. On the final day of the probe, the SIT also collected comprehensive details of the bank accounts of all accused and suspected individuals before returning to Lucknow with the assembled evidence. Records from 2021 also examined The SIT reviewed Mandir records dating back to 2021. Investigators examined expenditure details, utilisation of donation funds and land purchase transactions. Bank officials were also questioned during the probe. Sources said administrative action against Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr Anil Mishra is being discussed. Mandir construction in-charge Gopal Rao has also come under scrutiny. No official decision has been announced so far. ₹2 crore recovered so far Sources associated with the investigation said that cash and valuables worth around ₹2 crore have been recovered so far. The recovery was made based on information provided by five people linked to the Mandir's donation-counting process — Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune and Ram Shankar alias Tinnu. On June 13, gold was recovered from the residence of Mandir trust employee Tinnu. Officials have not yet disclosed the exact quantity. How the controversy began The issue first gained political attention on June 7 when former Samajwadi Party minister Pawan Pandey alleged that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from Ram Mandir offerings. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav later questioned the government's silence and demanded a judicial inquiry. Trust General Secretary Champat Rai denied the allegations and said no such matter had come to light. As the controversy grew, BJP leader Dr Rajneesh Singh wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 9 seeking a CBI investigation. The Prime Minister's Office reportedly sought a report from the Mandir trust the following day. Nripendra Misra calls it a serious failure Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Misra described the alleged theft as an "open loot" and called for a complete overhaul of the Mandir's management system. Speaking to a news channel on Friday, Misra said evidence related to the counting process pointed to weak monitoring and a lack of vigilance. He also questioned whether the responsibilities assigned to banking agencies were properly fulfilled. Yogi says guilty will not be spared Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited Ayodhya on Friday amid the controversy. After offering prayers at Hanumangarhi and Ram Mandir, he said the SIT would uncover the truth and that no guilty person would be spared. Yogi said the investigation was initiated following a request from the Mandir trust and urged people not to make irresponsible remarks that could hurt the sentiments of devotees. SIT investigation: Day-by-day timeline Day 1: The SIT gathered information from Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and invited member Gopal Rao. Around 8 to 10 Mandir employees suspected in the case were questioned for nearly six hours. Day 2: Champat Rai and Gopal Rao were questioned separately for about four hours each. Day 3: Investigators questioned bank officials and representatives of the private agency involved in counting donations. Bank statements and financial records were examined. Day 4: Trustee Dr Anil Mishra was questioned for nearly four hours. Investigators examined the donation-counting system, bank deposit procedures and appointments related to the counting process. Tinnu Yadav was also questioned and his statements were cross-checked. Day 5: Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao were questioned separately. The interrogation lasted around six hours. State Bank officials, including the branch manager and cashier, were also questioned. Day 6: The SIT collected details of the bank accounts of all accused and suspects, compiled evidence and returned to Lucknow. CEO proposal under consideration Sources said the government and Mandir trust are considering appointing a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for Ram Mandir, similar to the administrative model followed at Kashi Vishwanath Mandir. A senior IAS officer could be given responsibility for overseeing financial management, administrative operations and transparency in handling donations. Discussions are currently underway and no final decision has been taken. Claim over missing gold and silver bricks Dharmasena founder Santosh Dubey has alleged that around 1,250 gold, silver and ashtadhatu bricks, which were sent to Ayodhya after religious ceremonies across India and abroad in 1989, are now untraceable. According to him, these bricks were kept at Karsevakpuram until 2002. While clay bricks remain there, the metal bricks are allegedly missing. He has demanded an inquiry into the matter.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust set for major shake-up:Written accountability for all; Champat Rai and others may get new roles
stories.summary: The alleged donation theft case at Ayodhya Ram Mandir has prompted discussions on a major overhaul of the temple's management system. Sources said the arrangements for counting offerings, managing temple assets and handling darshan operations may be reorganised. Experienced administrators and Sangh-linked functionaries could be given greater responsibility in the trust and temple administration. The review gained momentum after questions were raised over the handling of donations. Sources said that despite the trust being formed on the directions of the Supreme Court, the responsibilities of trustees have never been formally defined in writing and no clear division of work exists within the organisation. Command may go to experienced officials According to sources, a new administrative structure is being prepared for temple operations. The duties of every officer and employee will be clearly defined in writing. A proper chain of command will also be established, specifying who is responsible for which task, who reports to whom and who will be accountable for decisions. The proposed system will not be limited to employees. The roles of all trust members and ex-officio members are also expected to be formally documented. Work related to donation counting and financial transactions may be distributed among several people instead of being handled by one individual. The aim is to reduce the possibility of irregularities in the future. SOP likely after SIT report Sources in the trust said a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for temple management, financial transactions and protection of assets will be prepared after the Special Investigation Team (SIT) submits its report. The SOP is expected to clearly define responsibilities and ensure that decision-making powers are not concentrated in one person's hands. Sources said preliminary work on the SOP has already started. Around 1,500 people are currently employed at the temple. A large number of them are associated with the RSS. While they receive salaries from the temple, their accountability has not been formally defined in writing. Temple Construction Committee chairman and trust ex-officio member Nripendra Mishra has also acknowledged this issue. Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao's roles may change Sources said senior RSS leaders have become active after questions were raised over the handling of donation money. The Sangh is waiting for the SIT report, after which accountability may be fixed. Key trust figures, including Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao, may either be removed from their current positions or assigned new responsibilities. Some new faces may also be inducted into the trust and management system. However, some Sangh functionaries believe Gopal Rao has served the temple for a long time and his commitment is not in question. They are reportedly keen to ensure that any change in his role is not seen as linked to financial irregularities or embezzlement. The SIT, which spent six days in Ayodhya investigating the donation theft case, is expected to submit its report to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday. Nripendra Mishra points to lack of accountability Nripendra Mishra, chairman of the Temple Construction Committee and an ex-officio trust member, has also raised concerns about the temple's management system. Speaking to the media, he said there is no fixed accountability for trust members and no formal distribution of responsibilities among them. At the same time, he defended trust general secretary Champat Rai, describing him as loyal and dedicated to the temple. Mishra has been one of the most active ex-officio members of the trust. His remarks have triggered questions about why these shortcomings did not come to light earlier. When asked about this by Dainik Bhaskar, he declined to comment further before the SIT report is released. Proposal for a Vaishno Devi-style board Sources said bureaucratic circles have also become active after questions emerged over temple management and financial oversight. Some retired and serving officials are reportedly in favour of appointing a retired or serving IAS officer as the temple's Chief Executive Officer (CEO). They have suggested creating a separate administrative office to oversee temple operations. Officials are citing the model of the Vaishno Devi Shrine Board as an example. If such a system is adopted, the temple's administration would come under a more structured framework with greater involvement of government-appointed officials.

stories.title: Ram Mandir offerings drop over 90% after donation theft row:Collections shrink from ₹12 lakh to ₹1 lakh a day; footfall remains unchanged
stories.summary: A donation theft controversy at Ram Mandir has triggered fresh concerns over how devotees' contributions are handled. The impact is now visible in donation box collections, which have fallen sharply even as the flow of devotees remains steady. Earlier, donation boxes at the temple used to receive ₹8 lakh to ₹12 lakh a day. According to temple employees, collections have dropped to below ₹1 lakh a day since the controversy surfaced. Temple authorities, however, say there has been no decline in the number of devotees visiting the shrine. Many devotees say the allegations have shaken their confidence in the donation system and made them favour online donations over cash offerings. Following the SIT investigation, the trust has tightened surveillance and strengthened the process of counting donations and depositing them in banks. The controversy has also brought back memories of earlier allegations linked to Ram Mandir funds, including claims of overpriced land purchases and questions over the use of donations. Devotees express concern, seek transparency Devotees visiting the temple say their faith in Lord Ram remains strong, but the allegations have raised concerns about how donations are handled. Shailendra Awasthi says devotees will continue to visit Ram Mandir from across the world, but the alleged theft has saddened many. He believes online donations are a safer option. Tarun Gupta, who visited Ayodhya from Delhi with his family, says the controversy has sent a wrong message. He says devotees should continue donating, but funds should also be used for facilities such as drinking water and assistance for the poor around the temple. The concern is not limited to devotees. Hanumangarhi Mahant Mahesh Yogi says the allegations have hurt the sentiments of Ram devotees and raised questions about whether donations and valuables are being used properly. He has demanded an impartial investigation and strict action against those found guilty. Aroma Gupta, another devotee from Delhi, says faith remains unaffected and that those responsible will eventually face the consequences of their actions. How donations changed over the years 2020-2024: Average donations touched ₹2.43 crore a day After the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was formed on February 5, 2020, a large-scale donation campaign began. According to trust figures, donations crossed ₹1,511 crore by February 2021. By the Pran Pratishtha ceremony on January 22, 2024, donations from all sources — including online contributions, donation boxes and the Har Ghar Samarpan campaign — had reached around ₹3,500 crore. This translates into an average of about ₹875 crore annually, ₹72.9 crore monthly and nearly ₹2.43 crore per day. At a trust meeting on August 22, 2024, officials said devotees had also donated 13 quintals of silver and 20 kg of gold. Even after construction expenses, around ₹2,600 crore remained in the trust's accounts. 2024-2025: Daily offerings fall to around ₹36 lakh Following the Pran Pratishtha ceremony, the temple witnessed a surge in footfall. Donation boxes alone collected more than ₹11 crore in the first 11 days, while total offerings crossed ₹25 crore in the first month. However, the pace slowed over time. Between January 2024 and March 2025, the temple received ₹153 crore in donations. This worked out to around ₹10.9 crore per month or ₹36.4 lakh per day. During the same period, the trust earned ₹173 crore as interest on its deposits. 2025-2026: Donation boxes contribute ₹16.6 lakh daily Accounts presented at the trust meeting on March 21, 2026, showed that between April 2025 and February 2026, the temple received ₹82 crore in donations. The average worked out to ₹7.45 crore a month and nearly ₹24 lakh a day. Of the total amount, ₹54.79 crore came through donation boxes, ₹18.88 crore through counters, ₹8.33 crore online and ₹78 lakh from devotees abroad. Donation boxes alone contributed around ₹16.6 lakh a day. The trust also earned ₹138 crore as interest from deposits in SBI, PNB and Bank of Baroda, taking total income to ₹221 crore during the period. Sources claim several people later accused in the donation theft case were recruited during this phase. June 15-19, 2026: Daily collections drop below ₹1 lakh Temple employees involved in counting donations say the controversy has had an immediate impact. According to them, donation boxes that earlier yielded ₹8-12 lakh on normal days are now generating less than ₹1 lakh a day. Between June 15 and June 19, daily collections reportedly ranged between ₹85,000 and ₹95,000. Officials say the decline is limited to donations and has not affected footfall. The controversy surfaced on June 7, when around 1.21 lakh devotees visited the temple. Similar numbers have continued to arrive since then. Donation counting system tightened Sources say the trust has increased vigilance after the controversy. Offerings continue to be counted under the supervision of trust member Anil Mishra at the basement of the Yatri Suvidha Kendra, located around 200 metres from the temple complex. Subhash Srivastava, a retired banker from Ayodhya, maintains the accounts. The temple has 35 donation boxes, all of which are now opened twice a day. Four representatives from the trust and banks remain present during the process. Counting is carried out in two shifts — from 8 am to 2 pm and from 2 pm to 8 pm. Around 20 people work in each shift, including permanent bank staff and outsourced employees. Sources claim some outsourced workers were hired on the recommendation of trust members. Several have reportedly been questioned by the SIT. stories.title: Govt removes lawyer in Azam Khan case:Handles trial for 6 years; services of 5 more lawyers end in Rampur
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has terminated the services of six government lawyers in Rampur, including those who were representing the state in cases against SP leader Azam Khan. Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi has also issued orders relieving the lawyers of their duties. The advocates removed are Amit Kumar Saxena, Sandeep Saxena, Pramod Sagar, Omprakash Lodhi, Pratap Singh Maurya and Amit Kumar. Among them, advocate Sandeep Saxena is considered to be very close to BJP MLA Akash Saxena. Special Secretary of State Government issued a letter It is being reported that letters were issued by the Special Secretary of the State Government to dismiss the lawyers. Following this, the DM issued the order. The sudden action has sparked discussions from Rampur Kachehri to Lucknow. After the government's action, Azam Khan's troubles may increase. Sandeep Saxena had advocated in several high-profile cases During his tenure, lawyer Sandeep Saxena represented the government in several high-profile cases against Azam. These included the 2 birth certificate cases, the passport case, lawsuits related to enemy property, and cases related to controversial statements against army personnel. Sentenced in 2 birth certificate cases Advocate Sandeep Saxena said that Azam Khan was sentenced in 2 birth certificate cases. Abdullah Azam was acquitted by the Sessions Court after being sentenced by the lower court in the passport case. The accused were also acquitted in the case involving controversial remarks against army personnel. Three lawsuits related to enemy property are currently pending in court. He stated that he had been working in this position for about 6 years. He does not know the reason for his removal. Lawyers said - This is part of governance Pramod Sagar, who was a government lawyer for about 7 years, refused to say anything in this matter. Meanwhile, Omprakash Lodhi called it a part of governance. He said that such decisions keep happening. Pratap Singh Maurya also said that he did not know the reason for his removal. Meanwhile, lawyer Amit Kumar said that he had been in this position for only two and a half years, while many lawyers remained in this position for 20-20 years. Azam had come out of jail for 55 days last year In 2022, Azam was sentenced to 3 years in a hate speech case, but in 2023, he was acquitted in the same case. Subsequently, in 2023, Azam Khan, his wife Tanzim Fatima, and his son were sentenced to 7 years each in the fake birth certificate case of his son, Abdullah Azam. Due to this conviction, he also lost his membership of the legislative assembly. After spending about 23 months in jail, he was released on bail from Sitapur Jail on September 23, 2025. However, just 55 days later, he was again sentenced to 7 years in the fake PAN card case of his son, Abdullah. Subsequently, he was sent back to jail along with his son.

stories.title: Answer key for UP police constable recruitment out:Objections invited till 23 June; 32,679 vacancies to be filled
stories.summary: The UP Police Recruitment Board has released the answer keys for all 6 shifts of the written examination for Constable recruitment. If you have any doubt about a question or answer, you can raise an objection within the stipulated time frame. All these documents have been made available on the board's official website. UPPRPB has advised candidates to rely only on the information provided on the official website https://uppbpb.gov.in. Candidates can log in using their registration number and password, select the exam date and shift, and then match their question paper and answer key. Exam was held from June 8 to 10 The written examination for constable recruitment was held on June 8, 9, and 10. The examination was conducted in 2 shifts on all three days. Thus, the examination was held in a total of 6 shifts. Now, the question papers and corresponding answer keys for all shifts have been uploaded on the official portal. Objections can be filed until June 23 The board has also started the process for candidates to register online objections. Candidates can register their objections from June 20 to midnight on June 23. No objection will be considered after the stipulated deadline. Objection must be submitted with evidence While registering an objection, candidates will be required to present solid evidence in support of the relevant question or answer. For this, relevant textbooks, official sources, or other valid references will need to be uploaded. Objections without proof will not be considered. According to the board, a panel of experts will examine the objections. If an error is found in any question or answer, a revised answer key will be released. If necessary, candidates' marks may also be revised. Now know about the recruitment On the evening of December 31, the Yogi government had issued a notification for direct recruitment to 32,679 posts. These included posts in Civil Police, PAC, Special Security Force (SSF), Women's Battalion, Mounted Police, and Jail Warder. In Civil Police, 10,469 posts will be recruited for female and male candidates. Whereas in PAC, there are 15,131 vacant posts for men. In UP SSF, there are 1341 vacancies for male candidates. The examination was conducted for three days (June 8, 9 and 10). For which a total of 1183 examination centers were set up in all 75 districts of the state.

stories.summary: After a woman died in a road accident in Mau, a commotion broke out. An angry mob placed the woman's body on the road and blocked the National Highway. The commotion lasted for about an hour and a half. Police tried to persuade the people, but they did not comply. When the police tried to remove the woman's body, an altercation with the police began. As the situation escalated, protesters started pelting stones at the police. Policemen ran to save their lives. Upon the arrival of reinforcements, the police began to disperse the protesters. They were also beaten. Stones were also thrown by the police. The incident occurred near Pidwal Bazaar in Ghosi police station area, on the Varanasi-Gorakhpur Highway. People say that road accidents occur frequently at this spot. Many lives have been lost. Their demand was for an underpass to be built in the market. People allege that despite the demand for an underpass, the road was constructed. To get from one side of the market to the other, people, especially women, have to cross the highway, which is constantly leading to accidents. People are angry that neither an underpass is being arranged nor any alternative facility for crossing the road, such as a footover bridge, is being provided. See pictures of the ongoing commotion

stories.title: Lucknow weather changes suddenly, rain lashes some areas:Power cut, bright sunshine in half the city; heatwave alert
stories.summary: The weather changed in Lucknow in the afternoon. There was strong sunshine since morning, while around 2 PM, rain started in some areas. Strong winds also began to blow. It started raining in Gomtinagar and Chinhat areas. The rain stopped in 10 minutes and strong sunshine emerged. During this time, areas like Hazratganj and Old Lucknow remained sunny. The Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave alert for today, Saturday. The Meteorological Department estimates that today Lucknow's maximum temperature will be around 42 degrees and the minimum temperature around 30 degrees. The Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave warning for the next 4 days (June 20, 21, 22, 23). 3 pictures of the changed weather- Now 2 pictures of dry areas Advice not to go out unnecessarily The Meteorological Department has also advised not to leave home unnecessarily. On Friday, Lucknow's maximum temperature was 41.3 degrees. This was 3.3 degrees higher than normal. The minimum temperature was 29.8 degrees. This was 2.8 degrees higher than normal. Maximum humidity was recorded at 62 percent and minimum humidity at 33 percent. Hot gusts of wind will continue The weather in Lucknow remains clear. Meanwhile, the mercury is continuously rising. Hot gusts of wind have been blowing since morning. The Meteorological Department estimates that Lucknow's maximum temperature will increase by 2 to 3 degrees in the coming days. This could lead to the mercury being recorded at its maximum level for the month. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that there is a possibility of light rain and scattered showers with thunder and lightning in some parts of the state. Despite this, the temperature will continue to rise for the next 5 days. Heatwave conditions will persist. Currently, the conditions are not favourable for the monsoon to arrive in UP and Lucknow.
