stories.title: Hamza from Gonda becomes Hemant Singh:Says he is a devotee of 'Mahadev'; claims his ancestors are Hindus
stories.summary: A youth from Gonda has claimed that he voluntarily converted from Islam to Hinduism in Lucknow and changed his name from Hamza Ali to Hemant Singh. He said he has been a devotee of Lord Shiva since childhood and has always worshipped him. He also claimed that his ancestors were Hindus who were converted during the Mughal era. On Saturday, the Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad organised a purification ceremony for Hamza and a woman at its office in Gomtinagar, Lucknow. The ritual was conducted by the organisation's national president, Gopal Rai. Rai said that two more people, whom he described as victims of 'love jihad', have approached the Parishad for help through its helpline. He added that the organisation will extend assistance to them. Whether my family accepts it or not, I am accepting it. The young man from Gonda said, Earlier I was Hamza Ali. Now my name is Hemant Singh. Our ancestors were Hindus and Sanatanis, but when the Mughals came, they forcibly mixed things up. I have had faith in Hinduism from the beginning. Whether my family accepts it or not, I am accepting it. My father's name is Hamid Ali Raini and my mother's name is Uma Anjum Raini. When I was coming back home (returning to my original faith), my family tried to persuade me. I am an adult, I can make decisions for myself. That's why I came back home (returned to my original faith). I have stopped offering Namaz for the last 5-6 years. Sometimes I used to offer Friday prayers (Jum'ah Namaz). I never went to a Madrasa, nor did I read the Quran, nor did I fast (Roza). I want my family members to also return (to the original faith). I perform worship, and I will always continue to do so The woman from Barabanki said- My name was Shabnam. After reconversion, I have become Sanjana. Shabnam said that I am changing my religion. Without any pressure or coercion, I am voluntarily leaving Islam and adopting Hinduism. I have had faith in Hinduism since childhood. I perform worship and will always continue to do so. I never read the Quran nor did I follow Islamic practices. 'Jihad victims from every corner of India are calling' Council President Gopal Rai said that the Sanatan Helpline is being run by the organization. On its numbers, victims of Love Jihad and Land Jihad from every corner of India are contacting, and 'Ghar Wapsi' (homecoming) is also taking place. Shabnam from Barabanki has now become Sanjana. Meanwhile, Hamza Ali from Gonda has now become Hemant Singh. Wherever in the world a person has been forcibly converted, we are facilitating their 'Ghar Wapsi'. We cannot carry out religious conversions; we do not have that right, which is why we facilitate 'Ghar Wapsi'. We were the ones who exposed the mastermind of conversion, Jamaluddin alias Jhangur, and had him sent to jail. Will hold a national conference on June 28 at the Bangladesh border Gopal Rai informed that the Sanatan Helpline number is helping all the victims. People are continuously contacting it. We are going to hold a national-level conference on June 28 at the Bangladesh border in West Bengal, where Sanatan culture will be promoted and propagated. It is the result of our hard work that the anti-Sanatan government in West Bengal was ousted and a BJP government was formed.

stories.title: NEET re-exam mock drill continues in UP:3.5 lakh candidates to appear on 21 June; bus fares cut by 50%
stories.summary: Ahead of the NEET-UG 2026 re-exam, the National Testing Agency (NTA) conducted a mock drill across Uttar Pradesh on Saturday to check exam arrangements. Multi-layer security has been put in place with the support of the police, district administration and central agencies to ensure the examination is conducted in a secure and transparent manner. Ahead of the exam, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also reviewed the preparations and directed the police and district administration to make foolproof arrangements for the smooth conduct of the test. In a major relief for candidates, the Uttar Pradesh government announced a 50% discount on fares in Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) buses. NEET candidates can avail of the concession by showing their admit card while travelling. Additionally, instructions have been given to arrange temporary accommodation for candidates travelling to other districts for the exam. After the NEET paper leak, the exam is scheduled to be held again on June 21. 3.5 lakh candidates will appear for the exam in 59 districts of the state. According to NTA, the exam will be held in pen-and-paper mode from 2 PM to 5:15 PM. Eligible candidates from PwD and PwBD categories will be allowed to write the exam until 6:20 PM, with additional time provided. Use of Aircraft for Paper Transportation According to officials, all exam-related tasks such as question setting, translation, printing, packaging, storage, transportation, and distribution are being closely monitored. The government will use Indian Air Force aircraft to transport all materials related to the question papers. Officials in the digital sector are keeping a 24-hour watch on social media platforms and messaging to keep fake question papers, misinformation, and suspicious activities away from the exam. NEET Exam 2026 was canceled on May 12 The NEET UG Exam 2026 was held in 551 cities across the country and 14 cities abroad. 22 lakh students participated in this exam. The NEET UG 2026 exam was cancelled due to a paper leak. Protests against this malpractice took place across the country. According to NTA, information about irregularities in the exam was received on the evening of May 7. Subsequently, the matter was handed over to central agencies. The exam was cancelled on May 12, and a decision for a re-exam was taken. Candidates should keep these things in mind before leaving home for the exam NTA has stated that keeping in mind the heat and the large number of candidates, arrangements for power backup, adequate lighting, fans, wall clocks, drinking water, toilets, and medical assistance have been made at all exam centers. According to NTA, candidates will be allowed to bring transparent water bottles. Diabetic candidates will be allowed to bring sugar tablets and fruits like bananas, apples, or oranges. Meanwhile, candidates wearing religious or traditional attire, and those wearing full-sleeve or woolen clothes, have been advised to arrive earlier for the checking process. Appeal to avoid rumors, social media under surveillance NTA stated that social media platforms are being continuously monitored to prevent rumors and disruptions. The agency has filed complaints with 14C/MHA, CBI, and other cybercrime agencies, and action is being taken on suspicious activities. NTA has appealed to candidates to rely only on official information and avoid rumors related to paper leaks or exams. They have been asked to report information about suspicious messages and channels to NTA or cybercrime agencies. The agency has advised students to remain calm, trust their preparation, and to use mental health helplines like Tele-MANAS (14416) if needed. States' preparations for NEET Re-exam Gorakhpur: 200 additional buses have been arranged for the candidates. Additionally, two pairs of unreserved special trains will be operated. For traveling from Gorakhpur to Lucknow, the 05007 unreserved examination special will depart at 4:05 AM, reaching Lucknow at 10:00 AM. Meanwhile, the 05035 examination special will depart from Gorakhpur at 7:15 PM and arrive at Lucknow Junction at 1:10 AM. There will also be two special trains for candidates returning from Lucknow to Gorakhpur. The 05036 Lucknow-Gorakhpur examination special will depart at 4:40 AM and reach Gorakhpur at 10:05 AM. Additionally, train 05008 will depart from Lucknow at 7:15 PM. Kanpur: Approximately 26,000 candidates will arrive. Railways has prepared a temporary holding area towards the station's clock tower. Arrangements have been made for examinees to stay here by setting up tents. Two help desks have also been set up to assist passengers. Special train 05320 Kasganj-Rawatpur Exam Special from Rawatpur will depart from Kasganj on June 21st at 6 AM. It will reach Rawatpur at 11:05 AM. After the examination concludes, 05319 Rawatpur–Kasganj Exam Special will depart from Rawatpur at 7 PM and, taking halts at designated stations, will reach Kasganj at 12:30 AM.

stories.title: Dubai handler ordered attack on RSS office:Lucknow was next target after Ranchi; masterminds are operatives of Tehrik-e-Taliban Hindustan
stories.summary: The petrol bomb attack on the RSS office in Ranchi, Jharkhand, was a well-planned conspiracy. According to the police, there was also a plan for an attack in Lucknow afterwards. The arrested accused, Aman Ansari, provided this information during interrogation. According to the accused, the instruction to throw the petrol bomb came from Dubai. Avesh Rajput alias Rana and Sahjad alias Shahnavaz Alam alias Bhatti, operatives of Tehrik-e-Taliban Hindustan (TTH) based in Dubai, are its masterminds. After the attack on the RSS office in Ranchi on June 17, Aman Ansari alias Golu and Saif Ansari had left for Kanpur by train that same afternoon, but Ranchi police arrested both of them from Gajhandi station. Order to attack RSS office received from Dubai Accused Aman Ansari stated that in September 2025, he went to Mumbai for a job. There, an agent named Zishan sent him to Dubai. There, he got the job of making ACs in Marmum Star Technical Service LLC company. After the visa expiry date, the company's supervisor Ahmed Ali sent him back to Mumbai this year. After this, he returned to Jharkhand. After coming to Jharkhand, Ahmed Ali made him talk to Rana over the phone. During interrogation, the accused stated that Rana had asked him to prepare three youths to throw petrol bombs at the RSS office. In return, Ahmed had promised good money. Photo and Location Sent from Dubai According to the accused, Rana, who was in Dubai, sent a picture and location of the RSS office in Ranchi to his WhatsApp on the night of June 15. The accused claims that he was instructed to throw petrol bombs and set the office on fire. On the night of June 16, he, Saif, and their associate Sayam Sujan reached near the RSS office. Saif threw a petrol bomb, while Aman was recording the incident. The first petrol bomb did not explode, which was reported to Rana. Subsequently, Rana allegedly instructed them to throw a second petrol bomb. According to the accused, after throwing the second petrol bomb, an explosion occurred, and the three fled from there. During police interrogation, Aman also claimed that the next morning Rana called and told him to leave Ranchi and go to Kanpur. From Kanpur, they were instructed to go to Lucknow and carry out another incident. Mobile with Aman, Rana was operating WhatsApp from Dubai During police interrogation, accused Aman Ansari stated that he had taken a mobile phone and a SIM card with number 9334314899 from his friend Haider Ali. Haider had kept this mobile and SIM card as collateral from a youth residing in Lohardaga. When the youth did not return the money on time, Haider sold that mobile to Aman. According to the accused, he used this number to communicate with different people. Rana, who is in Dubai, created a WhatsApp account using the same number after June 10 and used it. During interrogation, Aman claimed that he had also provided the necessary OTP to Rana for creating the WhatsApp account. Plan was to fire first During interrogation, Aman Ansari stated that Rana and Bhatti wanted to spread terror by first resorting to firing. For this, there was a plan to allegedly transport weapons from Pakistan to Ranchi. According to the accused, he left on June 8 by the Tata-Amritsar Express to go to Amritsar, but boarded a train going to Anand Vihar in Daltonganj. After this, on June 10, he reached Amritsar and stayed at Raju Mehta's hotel. Aman claimed that after this, Rana called and informed him that weapons were not available and asked him to return. He left Amritsar on June 12 and reached Lohardaga by train via Delhi. Subsequently, the plan was allegedly changed, and Rana instructed to attack with petrol bombs. ATS raids on the accused's hideout The Jharkhand ATS team raided the houses of Saif Ansari and Aman Ansari in Lohardaga, as well as the house of Sayam Sujan in Ranchi, early on Friday. An ATS team thoroughly searched the houses of both accused in Lohardaga and meticulously examined the items present there. Following this, Saif Ansari's elder brother, Chand Ansari, was extensively interrogated. Meanwhile, several important questions were also asked to the mother of the accused, Aman Ansari. Another team reached Sayam Sujan's house at Karbala Chowk, Pathalkudwa, in the Lower Bazar police station area of Ranchi. There too, every part of the house was thoroughly searched.

stories.title: Massive fire erupts at CNG station in Varanasi:Spark during refuelling causes massive blaze with 40-foot flames; people escape narrowly
stories.summary: A CNG pump caught fire in Varanasi at 9:20 PM on Friday night. The fire was so fierce that flames rose up to 40 feet high. The accident occurred when a vehicle was being filled with CNG. In no time, the fire took a monstrous form. There was chaos at the scene. Employees ran to save their lives. The CNG pump is located near Karkhiav village on the Varanasi-Jaunpur Highway. According to initial information, the fire was caused by a gas leak and a short circuit in the vehicle. As soon as the information was received, 12 fire brigade vehicles and a police team reached the spot. Fearing a cylinder explosion, the pump and the surrounding 200-meter area were evacuated. Employees and vehicles parked there were also moved to a safe place. The fire was brought under control at 2 AM. See 3 pictures The emergency stop button was turned off Immediately after the accident, employees pressed the emergency stop button to shut off the gas supply from the main storage tank and compressor. After this, they sounded the alarm and ran outside. They kept shouting to close the manual master shut-off valve, so that the leaking gas would not ignite further. After much effort, the master shut-off valve was somehow closed. But by then, small pipes and cylinders had caught fire. Due to high gas pressure, flames were rising. The administration and fire brigade are engaged in controlling the situation. Seeing the high flames of the fire, nearby residents came out. Vehicle drivers passing on the highway also stopped. Water is being sprayed on the cylinders Directly spraying water on the CNG fire is having less effect. The gas has been cut off. Since the CNG cylinders have become hot after the fire brigade arrived, water is being sprayed on them to cool them down and prevent them from bursting (high-pressure blast). Employees sent 200 meters away from the pump All vehicles and employees present at the pump have been sent away. There is still a risk of cylinders bursting, keeping this in mind, the surrounding 200-meter area has been evacuated. No one is being allowed to stand near the boundary, road, or surroundings. More fire engines are being sent from the city. DCP Gomti Neetu Kadyan said- Immediate cognisance was taken of the fire incident at the CNG pump located in Karkhiaon. Fire service personnel are engaged on a war footing to control the fire. Local police are also cooperating in relief and rescue operations while maintaining security. Rajesh Agarwal and Kaustubh Agarwal of BD Venture Group said- Even before the fire brigade arrived, water was continuously supplied from their hydrant system, which is greatly helped to prevent the fire from spreading.

stories.title: Hardoi BSA booked in ₹5 lakh bribery case:Claims DM 'trapped him in setup', cites earlier insults, abuses and threats
stories.summary: In Hardoi, FIR has been registered against Basic Education Officer (BSA) Dr Ajit Singh on Friday night over allegations of demanding a ₹5 lakh bribe. He is accused of threatening to blacklist an organisation linked to educator recruitment and demanding ₹5 lakh. It is also alleged that the organisation’s chairman had already paid ₹2 lakh. However, BSA Ajit Singh has denied all allegations, calling them false. He said District Magistrate Anunay Jha has set a trap to implicate him. He claimed that the DM had earlier also levelled corruption allegations against him but failed to prove them. He further alleged that Additional District Magistrate Prafull Tripathi is also involved. He also said that he was insulted in meetings, abused verbally, and was even threatened that he should leave the district. Missing documents found in teacher recruitment case Just a day earlier, 61 original documents related to 29,000 teacher recruitment cases were found missing. Following this, on the instructions of DM Anunay Jha, a three-member committee reached the BSA office on Friday evening around 5 pm. The team included City Magistrate Sanjay Singh, SDM Sadar Sanjay Agrahari, and DIET Principal Ramendra Singh. The team conducted a detailed inspection of recruitment records, appointment files and other important documents. During the investigation, several key records were found missing. Considering the seriousness of the matter, multiple cupboards and two rooms containing recruitment-related records were sealed. Officials said a detailed investigation would be carried out and action would follow based on findings. FIR based on complaint of institution chairman The FIR was registered at Kotwali Nagar police station in Hardoi following a complaint by Om Prakash Tiwari, chairman of Ujjwala Seva Sansthan, located in Gonda’s Tarabganj. He said that his organisation was authorised for recruitment of 210 ECCE (Early Childhood Care and Education) educator posts across several districts in Uttar Pradesh. He claimed that through the employment portal, 4,590 applications were received, and out of these, 630 candidates were shortlisted through randomisation by the district selection committee, and related data was obtained for further processing. He alleged that after about six months, when he contacted officials to proceed further, the BSA called him to the office and demanded ₹5 lakh as bribe. He further alleged that he was threatened that if the money was not paid, the organisation would be blacklisted and the security deposit would be forfeited. He also claimed that under pressure he paid ₹2 lakh, but even after that, demands for the remaining amount continued and harassment kept going on. BSA’s counter allegations BSA Dr Ajit Singh said the entire case is a trap laid by the District Magistrate. He claimed that the DM had been continuously accusing him of corruption but never proved anything. He said he was mentally harassed, abused in meetings, and told to leave the district. He further alleged that ADM Prafull Tripathi also harassed him. He said two clerks from his office were attached to the DM’s office, while two clerks from outside were posted in his office to monitor his activities. He stated that all actions related to educator recruitment were done under the instructions of the District Magistrate and under district administration supervision. Despite this, he is now being falsely implicated. He also alleged he was insulted in meetings and subjected to derogatory remarks. He claimed the DM called the firm operator and got a case registered against him as part of a conspiracy. He said ADM was also involved. He challenged the allegations, saying if he had taken any money, the candidates selected in the educator posts should be asked whether any illegal demand was made. He called it a well-planned conspiracy and said he would fight it legally. He also said he did not go to the office deliberately because he feared he would be falsely implicated and sent to police station. He added that one of his clerks had earlier been forcibly taken to the police station. Administrative action after missing recruitment files On the instructions of DM Anunay Jha, a team reached the BSA office and carried out an inspection after 61 original files related to 29,000 teacher recruitment were found missing. DM Anunay Jha is a 2015 batch IAS officer. During the inspection, officials checked recruitment and appointment records thoroughly. Some important files were found missing from the record. Considering the seriousness, cupboards and two rooms containing recruitment documents were sealed. Officials said a detailed investigation will be conducted and further action will be taken based on facts. 61 teachers’ original documents not found The investigation also revealed that original documents of 61 teachers related to the 29,000 teacher recruitment were not available in records. An FIR had already been filed against the then file in-charge Anupam Mishra. He was also responsible for the educator recruitment process.

stories.title: SIT back in Lucknow with Ram Mandir probe report:Action likely against Champat Rai, trustee Anil may also be removed
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the alleged Ram Mandir donation theft returned to Lucknow on Saturday evening after completing six days of inquiry in Ayodhya. The probe has identified around 150 suspects, with action likely against nearly 25 people. Sources said those questioned by the SIT have been instructed not to leave the city until further orders. On the sixth day of the investigation, the SIT examined records related to the use of donation funds, expenditure by the temple trust and land purchase transactions. The team also reviewed records dating back to 2021 and questioned bank officials. According to sources, the SIT has prepared a preliminary report, which is expected to be submitted to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday. Action likely against Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra Sources said action against Ram Mandir Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra is almost certain. Both may be removed from their posts. Temple construction in-charge Gopal Rao may also face removal. On Friday, the SIT spent nearly six hours inside the temple complex and questioned Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao separately. The team also wanted to question Somesh Anand, a temple employee and Gopal Rao’s nephew. However, he could not be located. Sources said his mobile phone has remained switched off. ₹2 crore recovered so far Investigators have recovered around ₹2 crore so far based on information provided by five accused — Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune and Ramshankar alias Tinnu. All five were associated with counting donations collected at the temple. Gold was also recovered from Tinnu’s house on June 13. However, officials have not yet confirmed the quantity of the seized gold. Allegations sparked political row Former Samajwadi Party minister Pawan Pandey had claimed on June 7 that between ₹5 crore and ₹7.5 crore had been stolen from the Ram Mandir. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the government's silence on the issue and said the matter should be examined by the courts. Responding to the allegations, Champat Rai had said no evidence of any theft had emerged. As the controversy grew, BJP leader Dr Rajneesh Singh wrote to the Prime Minister on June 9 seeking a CBI probe. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) sought a report from the temple trust the following day. How the controversy unfolded SIT questions donors in Ram Mandir offerings case; no receipt for silver gifts

stories.title: Rain hits 9 UP districts, heatwave alert in 24:Showers in Prayagraj Sonbhadra; monsoon likely by June 25
stories.summary: The fluctuation in UP's weather continues. Today, Saturday, there is a heatwave alert in 24 districts. There is a possibility of rain in 9 districts, including Saharanpur, Agra, and Jhansi. Clouds have covered most districts since morning. Due to the reduced wind speed, heat and humidity are being felt. Meanwhile, the monsoon has been delayed in the state. After reaching the UP-Bihar border, the monsoon has been stalled near Maharajganj for the last 5-6 days. The Meteorological Department (IMD) says that the monsoon will start advancing from June 23. If favorable conditions persist, the monsoon could enter UP by June 25. According to IMD, rain activities may continue in some parts of Southern UP for the next few days. However, this will not reduce the heat. Humidity will increase. Hot winds are likely to blow, and temperatures are expected to remain above normal in many districts of Eastern UP and Bundelkhand. Earlier, late on Friday night, heavy rain occurred in some areas of Prayagraj. In the morning, Farrukhabad and Kanpur experienced rain with strong winds for about an hour. People got some relief from the heat. Speaking of heat, Banda remained the hottest city in the country with 44.2 °C. Varanasi was second with 43.0 °C. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Kumar Singh, said, Seasonal activities in UP are currently limited to scattered levels. There is a possibility of light drizzle in some places, but this will further increase the heat. The mercury will continue to rise till June 24. The heatwave situation will become more severe. The pace of monsoon is also slow. Currently, conditions for monsoon entry have not been formed. One may have to wait at least 5 more days for the monsoon.

stories.title: UP ticket sale expose triggers political storm:Mayawati issues clarification, minister Nishad sets up probe panel
stories.summary: Following Dainik Bhaskar's ‘Ticket Deal Part 1’ and ‘Ticket Deal Part 2’ investigations exposing the alleged sale of MLA tickets, political parties scrambled to contain the fallout. BSP chief Mayawati issued a clarification on social media, while minister Sanjay Nishad announced a party-level probe. The Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Apna Dal (Sonelal) and Janwadi Party (Socialist) also moved quickly to limit the damage caused by the revelations. Actually, in Bhaskar's sting operation, BSP's UP President Vishwanath Pal demanded 5 lakh rupees for a meeting with Mayawati. He also quoted the rate for an MLA ticket as 3.35 crore rupees. After this sting was published, Mayawati clarified on her X handle, stating: BSP is a true and honest party that follows the path shown by Baba Saheb for the constitutional rights and justice of the Bahujan society. Other parties are trying to defame it.' Mayawati also reiterated her resolve to achieve the target of Mission 2027. Sanjay Nishad said - We have contested elections by supporting people Dr. Sanjay Nishad, National President of Nishad Party and Cabinet Minister in the UP Government, has formed a 4-member committee at the party level after Bhaskar's sting operation, which will investigate the demand for money in ticket distribution within his party. He said, We have contested elections with complete transparency. We have contested elections by providing support. Whatever comes to light, we will take action. On Bhaskar's camera, office bearers of Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar and Union Minister Anupriya Patel's parties were exposed demanding money in exchange for MLA tickets. Apart from them, Dr. Sanjay Singh Chauhan, National President of Janwadi Party (Socialist), which allied with SP in the last assembly elections, dealt to give a ticket for 2 crore rupees.

stories.title: Mathura's 'Shyam Guru' under police radar:Woman claims he hid first marriage, married her and abandoned home; now lives with third wife
stories.summary: A woman from Sewli village in Haryana's Palwal district has accused her husband of concealing his first marriage, then marrying her and later moving to Mathura where he allegedly adopted a new identity as a religious preacher. Pushpa, who has filed a complaint with Palwal SP Nitish Agrawal, said she married Ran Singh around 25 years ago. The couple have three children. She alleged that she discovered about one-and-a-half years after their wedding that Ran Singh had already been married and had hidden the information from her. ‘He left home and became Shri Shyam Guru’ According to Pushpa, Ran Singh left home around 10 years ago and moved to Mathura. There, he allegedly changed his name to "Shri Shyam Guru" and began working as a religious storyteller. She claimed that although he occasionally returned home, he never shared details of his activities or personal life in Mathura. Family learnt about another marriage while searching for him Pushpa alleged that the family later discovered that Ran Singh had married another woman in Mathura. She said the matter came to light when family members tried to contact him for financial assistance during their son's wedding preparations. After failing to reach him for a long period, relatives travelled to Mathura in search of him. According to the complaint, they found that he was living under a new identity and had started a family with another woman. Pushpa alleged that the couple also have a daughter. Claims ancestral land sold without family's knowledge The woman further alleged that Ran Singh used his claimed connections with influential political leaders to convince people that he could arrange jobs and resolve official work. She alleged that he collected money from people on these promises and that some of them later approached the family seeking refunds. Pushpa also claimed that he sold nearly one acre of ancestral land in the village without informing family members. Woman cites earlier criminal case In her complaint, Pushpa also alleged that Ran Singh had previously been jailed in connection with a rape case involving a woman from Naveepur in Uttar Pradesh. She said she chose to continue the marriage despite learning about the case because of family circumstances. Police hand probe to Mundkati police station Police spokesperson Sanjay Kadiyan said the complaint has been forwarded to Mundkati police station for investigation. "The allegations made in the complaint will be verified during the investigation. Further legal action will be taken on the basis of facts that emerge," he said. No response from accused Attempts were made to contact Ran Singh on three mobile numbers regarding the allegations. All three phones were switched off. Messages were also sent seeking his response, but no reply had been received till the filing of this report.

stories.title: Tourists going to Thailand returning as drug couriers:Peddlers receive at Lucknow Airport; 200 crore worth of cannabis seized in 2 months
stories.summary: A flight from Bangkok via Muscat arrived in Lucknow. Mohammad Imran was carrying 8.5 kg of hydroponic weed (cannabis). Imran was a resident of Mumbai. When he reached the immigration counter, the team became suspicious after seeing his travel history. During interrogation, it was revealed that he was a drug courier. He had to deliver the weed to someone in Lucknow. Actually, despite there being a direct flight from Bangkok to Lucknow, he was coming to Lucknow via Muscat. Whereas both the fare and time were more. When his passport was checked, it was found that he had made his first international trip just 6 months ago. He used to drive an auto rickshaw in Mumbai, after which he became a delivery man. Drug agents had given him the job of courier to bring goods from Bangkok without revealing their identity. He had gone from Mumbai to Bangkok. There he was given 17 crystal vacuum polybags wrapped in Camlin carbon paper. His luggage had reached Lucknow while evading X-ray machines in Bangkok and Muscat. The luggage contained 8.5 kg of hydroponic weed, which was worth 8.55 crore rupees. This is just one case, cannabis smugglers are adopting new tactics How is hydroponic ganja being smuggled? How are youth becoming carriers...read the complete report.. Being Made Drug Carriers by Offering Free Thailand Trip Durgesh (changed name) was caught with beads at Lucknow Airport. He had returned after a free trip to Thailand. Stay and food were all free there. He also received 15,000 rupees along with it. Recently, 4 youths were arrested at Lucknow Airport. Durgesh's name was also among them. When they were interrogated, they also revealed the free trip offer along with smuggling. Drugs worth two and a half crores were recovered from them. This incident is from September 2025. Sources connected to the Customs Department reveal that drug smugglers are ensnaring common people, especially youth, in this trade without taking risks themselves. They are executing drug trafficking while keeping themselves behind the curtain. Young people are getting trapped in this due to the lure of free trips. Durgesh was also just 30 years old. He had gone to visit Thailand. It was here that he fell into the smugglers' trap. This is not the first case. International drug networks are continuously ensnaring youth in their web by offering similar deals and commissions. This is the reason why Lucknow has emerged as a new route for hydroponic weed trafficking. Many youth who went to visit Thailand from here are returning as drug couriers, knowingly or unknowingly. Girls trap people into drug syndicate by befriending them According to airport sources, girls are also involved in this nexus in Thailand. Such girls roam around clubs and markets and trap boys who have gone there for leisure, running the drug syndicate. Many young men don't consider this a serious crime initially. They are told that it is legal there, it's just a herbal product, or 'no one will catch you.' In one case, a group of young people who went to Bangkok for a trip returned with packets in separate bags. Each young person was only told to bring their share of the bag. They just had to hand it over to the peddlers outside the airport. Later, during airport inspection, it was discovered that hydroponic weed was hidden in all the bags. The most shocking thing was that two minors were also included in the group. Investigation agencies believe that due to their young age, the network thinks there will be less suspicion from security agencies. 14 smuggling gangs identified, receivers meet outside the airport Airport sources say that the courier's real job is just to get out of the airport. Outside, a car and receiver are already present. Everyone has code names. These are the same names that agents give to the courier in Thailand. After this, they meet outside the airport. Many times the courier doesn't even know where the goods are ultimately going. The receiver has the description, photo and phone number, and after their flight arrives, the receiver themselves chases them. A young man arrested recently had told during interrogation that he just wanted a cut, meaning commission. He was told that if the first delivery was successful, then on every trip ahead you will get lakhs of rupees. I wasn't told whom to give these packets to, I was just told that a call would come after reaching outside the airport. In this work, minors traveling in groups are also being used. Due to the group, the suspicion of security agencies is reduced. In many cases, small quantities are kept in the bags of different members of the same group, so that there is not too much suspicion on any one person. Officials associated with the agency say that most of the hydroponic weed is being brought to Lucknow from Thailand via flights. So far, 14 smuggling gangs connected to this network have been identified. Smugglers are specifically targeting youth who travel abroad on tourist visas. The entire deal from the airport to safe delivery is pre-arranged. Network extends to hotels, beaches, restaurants; they even pack it in cookies According to investigating agencies, the entire drug network is operating in such a way that the real mastermind has not yet come to light. Whenever a smuggling case is caught, the courier is the first to be arrested, but not much is obtained from interrogating them because they don't know anything about the gang. This is why the people ordering the goods and running the network often escape. The smugglers' network extends to airports, hotels, beaches, and restaurants. They first conduct reconnaissance on such people, then make them couriers. Hydroponic weed has a high price in the international market and there is considerable demand for it in India, which is why its smuggling has increased. The methods of smuggling it are quite unique. One such case is from February 2026. At Lucknow Airport, officials laid a trap to catch smugglers. Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) officers spread out across the international terminal. Now they were waiting for the flight arriving from Bangkok. As soon as the flight landed, the AIU officers' circle tightened. Meanwhile, a young passenger was in customs' crosshairs. Sir, what's in your luggage? The nervous passenger started breathing heavily. He said, nothing... why do you think so? The customs officers pulled out cookie boxes from the luggage. The passenger quickly said... sir, it's packed, packed. It's cookies, I'll bring some for you next time too. Customs caught the passenger and seized the cookies. These cookie boxes contained hydroponic buds (marijuana). Its market value was around 2 crore rupees. 2 Thai women arrested with weed worth 20 crores Smugglers are using women as tools in this black market business. On April 6, 2025, two Thai women arriving from Bangkok were caught at Lucknow Airport. During investigation, approximately 20 kg of hydroponic weed worth around 20 crore rupees was recovered from their trolley bags. During interrogation, it came to light that both women were merely couriers and had to deliver to a network in India. Sources connected to the investigation say that drug smugglers have started using female travelers as tools to evade the eyes of security agencies. Our focus is also on Indian female travelers. Many youth are getting trapped in this web due to the lure of earning quick money, living a luxury life, and traveling abroad. But once arrested, serious sections under the NDPS Act are imposed on them, which have provisions for long sentences. Getting bail in such cases is extremely difficult. Now know about the smuggling route and supply chain- Currently only 40% of smuggling is being caught Gang not being caught, hence smuggling continues According to investigation agencies, the biggest reason for this is huge profits. Hydroponic weed purchased at low prices from Thailand is sold at several times higher prices in India. Its demand is rapidly increasing in big cities. Cannabis worth one thousand rupees there sells for approximately 25 thousand rupees here. Additionally, the networks use small couriers, so that the big kingpins don't come directly to the front. That's why even when couriers are caught, the entire gang remains active and continues smuggling by recruiting new people. They also keep adopting new tactics. In the international market, the price of one kilogram of hydroponic weed is said to be around one crore rupees. This is why it is also called the drug of the rich. Thailand's weed also gives a good high, which is why its demand is higher. Ganja worth 29 crores seized from Lucknow Airport Why is more coming from Thailand? Thailand legalized medical and to some extent cannabis in 2022. Following this, large-scale cultivation and sale of cannabis increased there. As a result, high-quality hydroponic weed became easily available there. Through international networks and tourism, its supply started reaching other countries. Taking it in and out of airports is also legal there. Therefore, weed is not caught in scanning either. Why are smugglers bringing more weed? Compared to regular cannabis, its price is several times higher. Supplies worth lakhs of rupees happen in small packets, so the profit is very high. Its demand is increasing in big cities, parties, and among high-profile youth. It has been given a premium drug-like image, due to which customers are willing to pay more. Its supply is also easy. In which countries of the world has it received legal approval? Many countries in the world have decriminalized cannabis, but have allowed its use with several conditions. Countries that have given approval include Argentina, Barbados, Chile, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cyprus, Denmark, Czech Republic, Ecuador, Finland, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Jamaica, New Zealand, Panama, Jamaica, Peru, Poland, Portugal and Israel among others. Several reasons have been given for approving cannabis here. Such as - its use in medicines and for research purposes. Cannabis has also been approved so that it can be used in diseases like severe pain, cancer and Parkinson's disease. What do legal experts say about cannabis? Former DGP of UP, Vikram Singh explains that cannabis is mainly considered to be of two types. Sativa and Indica. Both are used for medicine and intoxication. stories.title: 60 kg silver donation untraceable in Ram Mandir case:SIT records donors' statements, Mumbai family alleges no receipt issued
stories.summary: In the Ram Mandir donation theft case in Ayodhya, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) is now contacting devotees who handed jewellery or valuables directly to employees of the temple trust. The SIT is examining when the items were submitted, who received them, and whether any official receipt was issued. On June 18, the SIT recorded the statement of Mumbai-based businessman Anil Vishwakarma. He alleged that his family donated a 3-kg silver garland and a 1-kg silver charan paduka (sacred footwear) for Ram Lalla, but never received a receipt from the temple authorities. Another donor, Anurag Rastogi, North India Head of the Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association, claimed that there is still no trace of the 60 kg silver donated by traders through the association. Bhaskar spoke to both the donors and a local mahant regarding the matter. Family walked 200 km barefoot to offer silver garland and charan paduka Mahant Acharya Vinod Mishra of Ayodhya's Rokadiya Hanuman Temple said Anil Vishwakarma, originally from Jaunpur and now a businessman in Mumbai, had vowed to offer a silver garland and charan paduka to Ram Lalla. According to Mishra, the finely crafted silver garland weighed around 3 kg, while the charan paduka, engraved with 64 sacred symbols, weighed about 1 kg. He said the family, including women and children, walked nearly 200 km barefoot and reached Ayodhya on October 29, 2025. After worshipping the offerings at his ashram, they carried them on their heads to the Ram Mandir. Mishra claimed that at the temple entrance they met Ramashankar alias Tinnu Yadav, who escorted them to the sanctum sanctorum through the VVIP route. The offerings were placed before Ram Lalla and later taken into custody by Tinnu Yadav. Family says receipt was never provided According to Mahant Mishra, when the family later sought photographs of the offering and an official receipt, they were told that the silver would first undergo purity checks by bank officials before being used. On the issue of a receipt, Mishra said Tinnu Yadav allegedly told them it would be issued only after it was seen by "Bhai Sahab", a reference to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. Mishra alleged that neither the garland was placed on the deity nor was any information shared with the family. He claimed repeated requests for a receipt went unanswered. He further alleged that Tinnu later informed him the silver items had been sent to West Bengal to be melted and converted into silver bricks for making utensils required for temple rituals. "The devotee family felt deeply hurt after hearing this," Mishra said. Donor claims 60 kg silver donated during temple construction is untraceable Anurag Rastogi said bullion traders from across the country contributed small quantities of silver, ranging from 10 to 20 grams each, for the Ram Mandir project. According to him, a total of 60 kg silver was collected and melted into bricks weighing between 1 and 1.25 kg. The names and gotras of donors were inscribed on them. A 1-kg silver kalash was also donated by an association from Rishikesh. Rastogi said that on July 20, 2020, the silver bricks were taken to Ayodhya after receiving approval from Champat Rai. A worship ceremony was conducted at Ramkachehri, where Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and cashier Prakash Gupta were present. He claimed that Dr Anil Mishra and Prakash Gupta accepted the donation and issued a receipt along with a purity certificate. The association had requested that the silver be used during the temple foundation ceremony. Silver lamp and offering bowls also missing, says donor Rastogi said he had separately donated one 1-kg silver lamps, two silver bowls, a 200-gram panchdhatu pestle and a pair of Nag-Nagin idols. He claimed one of the silver lamps was used to light the temple's eternal flame by Dr Anil Mishra and his wife. The lamp was visible in photographs taken during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Ram Lalla. However, Rastogi alleged that after the completion of the grand temple, neither the silver lamp nor the silver bowls donated for offering bhog to the deity could be found.

stories.title: NEET student dies by hanging in UP:Writes suicide note to brother on question paper; aspired to become doctor like him
stories.summary: A NEET aspirant in Maharajganj died by suicide after returning home from her examination. She was found hanging at her residence while she was alone at the time of the incident. A suicide note was recovered from the spot, in which she reportedly wrote: “I cannot do anything, my dear brother.” Her family members rushed her to the district hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Following the information, police reached the spot. The student’s doctor brother told officials that the family had never pressured her regarding the exam or studies. He said they had always assured her that whether she got a government medical seat or not, her dream of becoming a doctor would definitely be fulfilled. At the hospital, the brother was seen crying inconsolably while holding his sister’s body. Now the complete incident in detail The incident took place on Monday afternoon in Choupariya Kanchanpur village under the Sadar Kotwali area. The brother, Abhinav Bharati, is a 2021 MBBS batch doctor. The deceased also aspired to become a doctor like him and was preparing for NEET. Abhinav said that his sister had appeared for the NEET exam on May 3, and her paper had not gone well. The family had been continuously reassuring her and motivating her to pursue other medical options like BAMS or private medical colleges if she did not secure a government seat. He added that due to ongoing controversy regarding paper leaks and re-exam discussions, she had been disturbed for the past month and was unable to study properly. Brother says he stepped out for 15 minutes According to the brother, on Sunday she had been checking answers from the exam answer key and became distressed, believing she might not succeed. Under this mental pressure, she took the extreme step. He further said that at the time of the incident, no one was at home. He had stepped out for around 15 minutes, during which the tragedy occurred. The father is a farmer and had fully supported her education and preparation. She was the only sister among two brothers. Her elder brother Abhinav has already cleared NEET in 2021, completed MBBS, and is currently doing internship at Deoria Medical College. Sadar SHO Nirbhay Singh said that the body has been sent for post-mortem. He added that the police are investigating the case from all possible angles, and further action will be taken after the post-mortem report.

stories.title: Tribute paid to deceased students in Lucknow fire:Congress district president demands inspection of coaching centres in Kanpur
stories.summary: Expressing deep sorrow over the untimely deaths of students in the tragic fire incident at a coaching centre in Lucknow, the Kanpur Metropolitan Congress, under the leadership of District President Pawan Gupta, organised a candlelight tribute at Tilak Hall. Under the leadership of District President Pawan Gupta, Congress workers lit candles and paid tribute to the deceased students. They also observed a two-minute silence and prayed for peace to the departed souls. On this occasion, those present expressed their deep condolences to the bereaved families and prayed to God to give them strength to bear this irreparable loss. District President Pawan Gupta said that the incident is extremely tragic and worrying. He stressed that safety standards in educational institutions must be strictly followed so that such painful incidents do not recur in the future. He also said that there are thousands of coaching centres in Kanpur and all of them should be inspected to ensure compliance with safety norms. He demanded a fair investigation into the incident and strict action against those responsible. A large number of Congress office-bearers and workers were present at the condolence meeting and all paid heartfelt tribute to the deceased students. Pawan Gupta, Harprakash Agnihotri, Hamdullah Malik, Ravi Tiwari, Padam Mohan Mishra, Rakesh Sahu, Pramod Gupta, Lallan Awasthi, Dharmendra Singh, Shankar Dutt Mishra, Haji Kausar, Ravi Bajpai, Raju Kashyap, Vinod Awasthi, Rajendra Valmiki, Mohammad Aftab, Brijesh Gupta and others were present.

stories.title: ₹11 crore gold purchase used to launder fraud money:Mumbai Crime Branch raids continue in Gorakhpur, hunt on for 2 suspects
stories.summary: A cyber fraud case that has shocked investigators has come to light in Gorakhpur, where a Mumbai-based gang allegedly used proceeds of fraud to purchase jewellery worth around ₹11 crore from multiple showrooms across the city. The accused first transferred money through online advance payments and then sent their associates to collect the jewellery. Since the payments were credited to the bank accounts of the jewellers on time, no suspicion was raised. A team from the Mumbai Crime Branch’s cyber cell is currently conducting raids and investigations in Gorakhpur, Deoria and Kushinagar. Searches are also underway for two suspected individuals linked to the case. Fraud routed through mule accounts According to information, cyber criminals did not use the fraud money directly. Instead, it was first routed through mule bank accounts. From these accounts, payments were then made to the bank accounts of well-known jewellery showrooms in Gorakhpur. As soon as the money reflected in the shopkeepers’ accounts, members of the gang would visit the stores and collect gold ornaments. Sources say this entire racket has been running for the past three months, with most purchases made from jewellery showrooms in the Civil Lines and Asuran areas of the city. Advance bookings used for delivery The fraudsters were highly organised. In several cases, they made advance online payments first and then sent their men the next day to pick up the jewellery. Since the payments were credited on time, shopkeepers did not suspect any wrongdoing. Mumbai Cyber Cell officials have so far visited at least four major jewellery showrooms in the city. Investigators are examining sale bills, documents and CCTV footage to identify the individuals who collected the jewellery and trace the wider network. Local youths allegedly hired on commission Investigating agencies suspect that the gang recruited several local youths in Gorakhpur and nearby areas by offering commissions. During the probe, the names of two suspects from Gopalganj (Bihar) and Deoria have surfaced. Police are now examining their bank accounts, mobile numbers and financial transactions to uncover the full network.

stories.title: 'Dad, there is fire, I am in bathroom, save me':Mother cries, pleads 'find my child', then faints; heart-wrenching stories of Lucknow fire tragedy
stories.summary: Dad, please save me. I won’t survive now. The fire has spread across the entire building. We have locked ourselves inside the bathroom. Smoke is also entering here. I am struggling to breathe,” the student said while crying on the phone. The father of the trapped student reached the spot immediately after receiving the call. He kept searching for his son in panic, showing his photograph to people and asking if anyone had seen him. Meanwhile, a mother who had reached the site fainted while pleading with others to help find her son. The building also housed a pet shop. Several pets, including dogs and cats, were trapped in the fire. As soon as a woman learned that her pets were inside, she broke down in tears. Parents of trapped students kept appealing to Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and officials with folded hands, requesting them to rescue their children. Father said - As soon as I got my son's call, I ran towards the coaching center Prabhujyoti Singh said his son made the distress call from inside the coaching centre. “My son Sukhmani Singh called me and said there is a fire, please save us. Then the call got disconnected. I immediately rushed here. On the way, I kept calling ambulances and the fire brigade, but I could not get through for a long time,” he said. He added that he has not been able to speak to his son again since then. His phone is switched off. While saying this, Prabhujyoti Singh broke down in tears. Mother said - Someone please find my child... Another student, Aditya Srivastava, was also reported missing after the incident. There was no information about him. He had reportedly called a friend saying he was trapped and needed help, after which he went out of contact. His friend informed his mother, who rushed to the site crying and asking everyone about her son. She kept pleading, “Someone please find my son… what will we do now?” Overcome with grief, she fainted on the spot. People present there helped her recover. Later, it was confirmed that Aditya Srivastava had died in the incident. Locked themselves in washroom to escape from fire Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak reached the site and spoke to students who were inside the building during the fire. They informed him that 3–4 students had locked themselves inside a bathroom to escape the flames. Fire brigade teams reached the upper floors and checked each room and bathroom one by one during the rescue operation. Coaching employee said- I climbed down holding the wire A coaching centre employee, Mohammad Asin, said that as soon as they got information about the fire, they ran outside. Smoke had filled the staircases and rooms. “I came down from the upper floor by holding onto a wire. Only then could I save myself,” he said. He added that initially he thought it was a small fire, but it quickly turned massive. Realising the danger, he escaped by climbing down using a wire. Woman kept crying to save her stomach A woman who reached the spot with her family said two of her pets were inside the pet shop in the building. When she could not get any information about them, she began crying uncontrollably and appealed to officials to save them as well.

stories.title: 15 dead in fire at Lucknow coaching centre:AC short circuit suspected as cause; 4 officers suspended, 3 accused arrested
stories.summary: A devastating fire tore through a building in Lucknow on Monday afternoon, claiming 15 lives. Most of the victims were students in their 20s and 30s attending a coaching centre on the second floor. The casualties include 10 men and 5 women. According to reports, after the fire spread, students locked themselves in the bathroom. One child jumped from the first floor to save his life, but fell onto the grill below and was seriously injured. CM Yogi has suspended four officers. An FIR has been filed against three of the accused and they have been arrested. Building housed a pet shop, coaching centre and game studio The building where the fire broke out is located in the Aliganj area. The basement, ground, and first floors house a pet shop and a clinic. The second floor houses a library called Learning Space (used as a coaching centre) and Head Hopper Studio, which handles 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. Short circuit suspected as cause The cause of the fire is suspected that it was caused by a short circuit in the AC system in the basement. Around 10 fire brigade vehicles are at the scene. The SDRF and NDRF have also arrived. Firefighters have broken down the rear wall of the building and are recovering bodies. Ambulances were insufficient to transport the dead and injured. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak, who was present at the scene, wept at the sight. He said, “I saw bodies being carried before my eyes.” PM announces ₹2 lakh relief Meanwhile, PM Modi announced that an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each deceased. The injured would be given Rs 50,000. Visuals from the incident: Location of the incident: Follow our live blog for regular updates…

stories.title: Wrestler sets herself on fire at Bijnor police station:Had earlier filed rape a case against a soldier; condition serious
stories.summary: A female wrestler set herself on fire at Kotwali city police station in Bijnor on Sunday night, protesting police inaction in an alleged rape case she had filed against a soldier. The incident occurred at 10:45 pm. As soon as the female wrestler was on fire, she started screaming and ran in the station. During this, the fire spread onto the curtains of the inspector's chamber. Police personnel present at the scene extinguished the fire and took the woman to the district hospital. Doctors administered primary treatment and referred her to a hospital in Meerut. Currently, the woman's condition is critical. Doctors said she has suffered 60 per cent burns. The police's initial investigation revealed that the female wrestler had a love affair with a soldier. It is alleged that the soldier had promised marriage but later backed out. Following this, the woman had filed an FIR against him for rape. The accused soldier had obtained a stay on his arrest from court, due to which the police were unable to take action against him. Angered by this, the woman took the extreme step. In this matter, SP Abhishek Jha has suspended station in-charge sub-inspector Amar Singh Rathore with immediate effect. Sequence of events The woman is 25 years old. She has studied M.Sc and also wrestles. Her father was a home guard. He died in a shooting incident at the DM's residence a long time ago. After this, her mother remarried. The woman has a brother. It is being said that three years ago, the female wrestler met Saurabh, a soldier from Bijnor, at Saraswati Vidya Mandir. After this, the two became very close. Saurabh had promised to marry the female wrestler, but later backed out. SP Abhishek Jha stated that the young woman had previously filed a rape case against Saurabh. Due to lack of evidence, the police had filed a final report in the case. After this, the young woman again filed a report against the young man, on which the police had filed a charge sheet in court. Saurabh had obtained a stay on his arrest from the High Court. Came to the police station in the afternoon, set herself on fire at night The female wrestler came to the city police station with her mother on Sunday afternoon. She demanded action against Saurabh. Police personnel explained to her the developments in the case and asked her to return home. After this, she again reached the police station on Sunday night and started demanding the arrest of the soldier. When the police personnel did not listen to her, she poured petrol and set herself on fire. Upon receiving information about the incident, there was a stir in the police department. SP Abhishek Jha and SP City Dr. Krishna Gopal Singh immediately reached the police station. SP Abhishek Jha said- The woman is about 60% burnt. Currently, she is undergoing treatment in Meerut. Upon checking CCTV footage, it was found that her stepfather Naresh had given the woman the bottle of oil.

stories.title: Fake tea tip-off uncovers major counterfeit goods racket:Counterfeit packing of Harpic, Fair Lovely and Eno seized in Gorakhpur; case registered
stories.summary: A major counterfeit goods racket has been uncovered in Gorakhpur during a raid linked to the fake packaging of Brookbond Taaza tea. During the operation, officials recovered not only counterfeit tea products but also suspicious packaging of several well-known brands, including Fair Lovely face cream, Harpic and Eno. The Food Safety Department has sealed the entire stock. Based on a complaint filed by a company representative, a case has been registered against shop owner Abhishek Kumar Gupta under the Copyright Act at Cantt Police Station. Officials posed as customers to trace the store The Food Safety Department had received information that counterfeit products of reputed companies were being sold in the city. However, officials were initially unable to identify the exact location of the store. To track it down, the team contacted the supplier while posing as customers and placed an order for tea leaves. Around six hours later, the delivery arrived at the designated address. Officials then accompanied the delivery person to a store in Bilandpur, where they discovered a large stockpile of suspected counterfeit goods. Counterfeit products found across multiple brands During the inspection, officials recovered suspicious packaging and products linked to several brands, including Brookbond Tea, Everest Masala, Cadbury Gems and Rajesh Masala. The seized items included- Samples of all recovered products have been sent for laboratory examination. Case registered following company complaint A case has been lodged at Cantt Police Station on the complaint of Amit Kumar Mall, Senior Investigator Officer at Check IP Solution Private Limited, Lucknow. Police and the Food Safety Department are jointly investigating the matter. Store operated quietly in residential area Company representatives had informed authorities that Brookbond Taaza tea was being sold in fake packaging in the Cantt area. Despite several attempts, officials were unable to locate the premises. After obtaining the supplier's mobile number, the department placed an order on Saturday morning. When the delivery arrived at around 6 pm, officials followed the delivery route and reached the store. Investigators were surprised to find suspected counterfeit products of several other companies alongside the fake tea packaging. Source of counterfeit packaging under investigation During questioning, the shop owner claimed he sourced the goods from Maharajganj. However, officials are not fully convinced by his statement. Investigators suspect the counterfeit packaging may have been manufactured elsewhere and supplied through the Gorakhpur outlet. Efforts are now underway to identify the wider network and locate the packaging unit involved. Crackdown on counterfeit goods to continue Food Safety Department officials said some traders are exploiting the names of established brands to sell fake products. They noted that previous raids in the Kotwali area had also led to the recovery of counterfeit packaging for products such as Tata Salt, tea leaves and Fevikwik. Authorities said their campaign against adulteration and the sale of counterfeit products will continue.

stories.title: 200-year-old Tazia brought out in Varanasi:Historic Mughal-Iranian design structure taken out for Muharram observances
stories.summary: The Tazia of Mote Shaban at the Baradari Imambara in Doshipura, Varanasi, was brought out from the Baradari Mosque and installed on the occasion of 6th Muharram (Monday). The 200-year-old Tazia has been taken out annually since 1981 after the seals on eight locks are opened in the presence of police and administrative officials. Hundreds of devotees gathered inside and outside the mosque during the process. The Tazia, which is stored in separate sections throughout the year, was carefully brought out piece by piece from the chamber (hujra) where it is kept. See pictures- History of the Tazia 200-year-old structure carried by 60 people Gulzar Ali said the Tazia is popularly known as the Tazia of his ancestor, Mote Shaban, who died in 1857. The structure predates his lifetime and was already being carried in religious observances before then. Mote Shaban was closely associated with the then Kashi Naresh, and since his era, the Tazia has been brought out from the mosque and installed at the Baradari every year on 6th Muharram. The Tazia is carried by around 60 people and consists of 22 individual sections, including five principal components. Among them is the main dome, which features silver and gold ornamentation. The structure is crafted from teak wood and decorated with intricate Mughal and Iranian-style designs.

stories.title: 70-foot slab of under-construction bridge collapses in Hardoi:Slipped while being lifted by crane, 2 labourers gets trapped
stories.summary: A 70-foot concrete slab of an under-construction bridge over the Sharda Canal in Hardoi collapsed on Monday morning, trapping two labourers beneath the debris. Both workers sustained serious injuries in the accident. The incident occurred while a crane was lifting the massive slab into position on the bridge under construction. Following the collapse, rescue teams used a crane and bulldozer to remove the fallen slab and free the trapped workers. The injured labourers, identified as Rahul (30) and Gendalal (35), both residents of Sidhauli, were rushed to the district hospital. After receiving primary treatment, they were referred to a medical college due to the severity of their injuries. DM orders investigation Hardoi District Magistrate Anunay Jha has ordered an inquiry into the incident. He said strict action would be taken against those found responsible once the investigation is completed. The bridge is being constructed by RCL Company as part of the Lucknow–Palia National Highway project. Residents claimed that a section of the same under-construction bridge had also collapsed around 1.5 months ago. Part of ₹600-crore highway project According to NHAI Assistant Engineer Pushpesh Yadav, the bridge forms part of a ₹600-crore highway project stretching from Shahabad to Khetui village in Hardoi district. An overbridge is currently being built near Saidpur village in the Behta Gokul police station area. Construction began in November 2023 and was scheduled for completion by November 2025. However, delays in shifting high-tension power lines have slowed progress. See 4 pictures related to the accident-

stories.title: 21-year-old SP office demolished in Sitapur:Bulldozer action begins at 4 AM; lease was granted during Mulayam's government
stories.summary: A Samajwadi Party (SP) office built on government land in Sitapur, UP, was demolished early on Monday morning. The district administration reached the spot at 4 am with forces from 5 police stations. Four bulldozers razed the office to the ground in 2 hours. The debris was also removed. During this, 25 policemen and 50 Pradeshik Armed Constabulary jawans remained deployed. Sadar SDM Dr. Janardan Kumar and several other officials were also present. The SP office was built 21 years ago on 2,500 square feet of land. The lease was given in the name of the SP office on government Nazul land. However, the lease was cancelled four months later. At that time, Mulayam Singh Yadav was the Chief Minister. Even after the lease was cancelled, the SP office continued to operate here. Fifteen days ago, the district magistrate's court had sent a notice to SP district president Chhatrapal Yadav. He was given time till Sunday to vacate the office. The SP district president had vacated the office 24 hours before the bulldozer action. Pictures of the bulldozer action- Sequence of events Seema Singh, the executive officer (EO) of the Municipal Council, said, "On January 15, 2005, the then Municipal Council president Radheshyam Jaiswal had allotted the Nazul land of the Town Hall complex for the SP district office. The rent for this was fixed at only ₹100.' She said, “A hall and two rooms were built on 2,500 square feet of land. However, within a few months, the allotment came under dispute. During the investigation, irregularities in the observance of rules and legal provisions in the allotment process came to light. The Municipal Council had cancelled the allotment on April 14, 2005.” SP MP says the BJP will have to bear the loss for this Anand Bhadauria, SP MP from Dhaurahra, said, “Legally, our side was weak in the office matter, but the way BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party) demolished the office by deploying bulldozers early in the morning, Samajwadi supporters will never forget it. The public will surely break BJP's arrogance. BJP will have to pay the price for this.” BJP district president says action against breaking of rules Rajesh Shukla, BJP district president of Sitapur, said the BJP government works in accordance to the law. “The administration will take action against anyone who violates the rules,” he said.

stories.title: 'Saifai family took money in Gomti Riverfront scam':Minister Rajbhar says, 'I am sitting with complete file, will reveal all secrets one by one'
stories.summary: Raising the political temperature in Uttar Pradesh, Om Prakash Rajbhar, chief of the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) and a cabinet minister in the Yogi government, once again launched a sharp attack on Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Monday. Rajbhar accused Akhilesh of diverting funds allocated for the Gomti Riverfront Project to finance the 2017 Assembly elections. He claimed that after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's demonetisation move, Akhilesh could no longer rely on the alleged black money of gangster-politician Atiq Ahmed, prompting him to use project funds instead. The minister also said he would expose alleged corruption during the SP regime "one file at a time". Read what allegations Minister Rajbhar made against Akhilesh Yadav... 'Entire budget spent, only 60% of work completed' Rajbhar alleged that despite the entire project budget being spent, only 60 per cent of the Gomti Riverfront Project was completed. According to him, funds meant for the remaining 40 per cent of the work ended up in the coffers of the "Saifai family" and were used during the Assembly elections. Taking a swipe at Akhilesh Yadav, Rajbhar said the former chief minister believed his alleged wrongdoing would remain hidden after returning to power, but "the cup of sin had overflowed". He added that the government of "scammers" lost power and the alleged irregularities subsequently came to light. 'No air Conditioning in jail, no press conferences either' Rajbhar described the Gomti Riverfront case as only one example of what he called corruption during the SP government. He claimed to possess several files related to alleged irregularities and said each case would be revealed in due course. He also stated that investigating agencies are probing the Riverfront Project and that the truth would soon emerge. In a sarcastic remark aimed at Akhilesh Yadav, Rajbhar said: Have patience. In jail, you will get neither air conditioning nor access to Twitter, and you will not be able to hold press conferences. What is the Gomti Riverfront project case? The Samajwadi Party government sanctioned ₹1,513 crore for the Gomti Riverfront Project. According to official records, ₹1,437 crore was released, yet only around 60 per cent of the work was completed. Despite nearly 95 per cent of the budget being disbursed, about 40 per cent of the project remained unfinished. Allegations were later made that tender conditions had been altered to favour a defaulting company. Around 800 tenders were reportedly issued for the project, with authority vested in the Chief Engineer. Yogi government ordered judicial probe After coming to power, the Yogi Adityanath government constituted an inquiry committee headed by retired High Court judge Justice Alok Singh to investigate the alleged scam. Based on the committee's findings, further action was initiated. In December 2017, the CBI registered an FIR in connection with the Riverfront Project. The FIR named eight individuals, including- Of the eight individuals named in the FIR, seven have since retired from government service. Cases were registered under provisions related to financial irregularities and alleged corruption. In July 2017, the Uttar Pradesh government formally recommended a CBI investigation. Along with the recommendation, it submitted the judicial inquiry report, a copy of the FIR registered at Gomtinagar police station and other relevant documents. Rajbhar repeats claim of imminent split in SP During the ongoing monsoon session, Rajbhar once again claimed that the Samajwadi Party is heading towards an internal split. Referring to the splits in the Trinamool Congress in West Bengal and the Shiv Sena in Maharashtra, he said the next political break-up would occur in Uttar Pradesh. Rajbhar claimed that a division within the SP would emerge during the monsoon session and would be led by what he described as the "rebel son of Ballia". He further alleged that Ram Gopal Yadav had submitted a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Rajbhar also claimed that Ram Gopal Yadav's son, Shivpal Yadav, his son, and several other family members were linked to the Gomti Riverfront case. Referring to Akhilesh Yadav's recent remarks that the BJP had poached SP legislators, Rajbhar said- Those who are weak and timid will leave. Apart from four or five family members, everyone is prepared to abandon him. SP leaders reject Rajbhar's claims Rajbhar's assertions have been dismissed by several Samajwadi Party leaders. More than 20 party MPs, including Ballia MP Sanatan Pandey, rejected the claim that the SP was facing a split. Even Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya described Rajbhar's prediction as baseless. Amid the war of words, a hoarding targeting Rajbhar appeared outside the Samajwadi Party headquarters in Lucknow. The hoarding was put up by SP leader Mohammad Ikhlaq Ahmed, who mocked Rajbhar's claims. Alongside Rajbhar's photograph, the message read- My own MLAs are roaming around carrying the SP flag, and I am talking about breaking the party. What answer will I give when the public asks questions? Ikhlaq Ahmed said that Rajbhar, Minister Sanjay Nishad, and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya have repeatedly claimed that the Samajwadi Party is on the verge of a split. He countered that Rajbhar's own MLAs openly identify with the Samajwadi Party and regard Akhilesh Yadav as their leader. Ahmed also targeted Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad, saying he entered mainstream politics and became an MP with the support of Akhilesh Yadav before later joining the ruling alliance.
